entries.name: agora
entries.description: Self-driving multi-agent development team. Role-based workers (architect, developer, reviewer, tester, researcher, writer, devops) are each a real Hermes profile with its own SOUL.md and skills; they discuss and vote on decisions, and the adopted conclusion is executed by the same team. A "leader" profile chairs the discussions and a heartbeat cron wakes it to assess state, unblock workers and plan the next phase. Discussion and execution share one board: a motion is a sub-task of a per-project team channel task, speech and votes are `[agora:msg]` comments, the conclusion is written to task.result, and an adopted conclusion becomes execution tasks parented to the motion so context reaches workers through Hermes' own parent handoff. Ships 20 tools, 3 kanban lifecycle hooks, a dashboard tab and an `qubit agora` CLI; installing writes nothing — the three bundled skills are deployed by an explicit `qubit agora setup`. Disclosure — creates a Hermes profile per worker, copying the global config.yaml and .env into it (a private copy, mode 0600, never a symlink to the real credentials); spawns `qubit -p <profile> chat -Q -q` subprocesses to speak in discussions and to run dispatched tasks, which execute as full agents with that profile's toolset, including terminal and file writes inside the project workdir. Those subprocesses receive `--yolo --accept-hooks` ONLY when the project opted in via `agora_start_project(allow_unattended=True)`; the default is off, so a freshly installed team can read, discuss and plan but its flagged writes and shell commands fail closed. Also reads and writes the kanban database (tasks, task_comments, task_events, task_runs, task_links) restricted to its own project boards, including a persistent team-channel task pinned in `scheduled` status, and deletes a project's own tasks when it stops or completes; registers one recurring cron job and writes its runner script to QUBIT_HOME/scripts/leader_heartbeat.sh; writes AGENTS.md into the configured project workdir; deploys three bundled skills into QUBIT_HOME/skills/collaboration/; and serves a dashboard tab plus REST routes through the Hermes dashboard. No network egress of its own — model calls happen inside the spawned Hermes subprocesses under the operator's own provider credentials.

entries.name: antigravity-agy
entries.description: Run Hermes on a Google Antigravity subscription through the official agy CLI, with agy as the model only: a generated custom agent removes agy's built-in tools, Hermes tools are exposed through an inventory-only MCP server with native function calling, and every tool call is handed back to Hermes. Fails closed on any non-Hermes tool step or silent agent fallback; pre-warms agy for fast tool loops. Disclosure — routes inference through Google's official agy CLI and counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to; the plugin never reads, copies or links agy's credential files. agy runs in your real HOME with the gateway's environment; by default the plugin moves the agy conversation records created by its own idle pre-warmed processes under ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/ to the trash (trash-put from PATH; ANTIGRAVITY_AGY_CLEANUP=off disables) and pre-warms up to 4 idle agy processes (~400 MB each).

entries.name: antigravity-oauth
entries.description: Sign in to Google Antigravity with `qubit auth add antigravity-oauth` (or one command, `npx qubit-antigravity-oauth`) and run Hermes on the Antigravity plan: Gemini 3.x, Claude 4.6, GPT-OSS. Every request is made by Google's official agy CLI under agy's own login. The plugin writes your Hermes SOUL.md and system prompt into agy's workspace GEMINI.md so the persona carries over. When a model reaches for an agy-native tool (run_command, view_file, grep_search, and so on) the call is re-issued as the matching Hermes tool, which then runs under Hermes approvals. agy never executes tools on the host, and unmapped native tools are blocked. Disclosure: inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin never reads, copies or uploads the OAuth token. It symlinks agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME, which is deleted on close. It also probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT). Disclosure — inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin does not read or upload the OAuth token itself; it symlinks (hard-links, or as a last resort copies) agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME that is deleted on close, probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only, and writes the full Hermes system prompt into that temp workspace as GEMINI.md each turn. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT).

entries.name: biomimetic-brain

Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package; it registers no hooks, no tools and no middleware, makes no network calls, and reads and writes state files only under the agent directory you choose, where a subsystem that has stopped updating reports stale instead of asserting an old number. No dependencies beyond the Python standard library (two shell scripts for the scheduled passes). Its scripts, when the agent or operator runs them, read and write JSON state under the directory chosen with MIND_AGENT_DIR (default an agent/ folder inside the plugin's own install dir), read QUBIT_HOME/cron/executions.db for cron counts, and execute scripts/batch-maintenance.sh or scripts/verify-invariants.py from that agent directory if present; no network egress and no LLM calls.

entries.name: chronicle
entries.description: Local-first long-term memory and memory-aware context compression for Qubit — SQLite, no account, API key or hosted service required. entries.name: commandcode-oauth

Live /model and Desktop catalog probing for non-api_key profiles depends on upstream PR 122203; hermes model setup already fetches the live account catalog.

entries.description: CortexLayer memory provider — page-linked long-term memory with link-expansion retrieval, wired into Hermes' automatic per-turn recall (prefetch) and persistence (sync_turn), plus a pre-compress checkpoint so evidence Hermes' own context compaction would otherwise drop is saved first. Platform mode only: each turn's query and conversational content is sent to the hosted api.cortexlayer.net (HTTPS, API-key authenticated) for storage/retrieval — no local/offline mode. Requires a free CortexLayer account and API key.

entries.name: covision
entries.description: Read-only Covision meeting, assigned-task, and published-knowledge tools through the Covision Streamable HTTP MCP service, plus a workflow skill. Requires a Covision account, organization connector enablement, and browser OAuth consent; no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin.

entries.name: crawl4ai
entries.description: Crawl4ai self-hosted web content extraction. Requires CRAWL4AI_URL and CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN pointing at your instance.

entries.name: cron-bulletin
entries.description: Central Qubit Desktop inbox for reports produced by local cron runs.

entries.name: crypto-prices
entries.description: Live crypto price ticker for the desktop status bar — Top 10 by market cap, seamless marquee, custom coins & 60+ display currencies, adjustable width (CoinGecko, no API key).

entries.name: custodian
entries.description: Autonomous operations monitor for a Qubit install: scans gateway logs, cron jobs, skill journals and agent data directories, classifies findings against a 27-fingerprint registry, auto-repairs Tier 1 problems, escalates the rest, and keeps an append-only issue ledger. Ships /custodian (status, scan, issues, repair, verify, schedule, confidence, init, escalation-runner), four scan/health tools and a grid dashboard. Disclosure — reads gateway logs, cron job state and per-skill journal files under QUBIT_HOME to build its findings, and writes repair actions and an issues ledger back there; it performs no network I/O and holds no credentials. Disclosure — /custodian init registers 3 recurring agent cron jobs (deep scan 4×/day, cron-health 4×/day, escalation runner every 30 min on weekdays).

entries.name: custom-dangerous-patterns
entries.description: Add custom dangerous command patterns to Qubit's built-in approval system. Users define regex patterns in YAML; the plugin injects them into DANGEROUS_PATTERNS at startup and registers a pre_tool_call hook to enforce deny patterns.

entries.name: dashboard-auth-ldap
entries.description: LDAP / Active Directory password login for the web dashboard. Verifies credentials with an LDAP bind (direct or search-then-bind), never stores passwords, requires ldaps:// or StartTLS, and supports group restriction. Registers the `ldap` dashboard auth provider once dashboard.ldap_auth is configured. Disclosure — dashboard logins are verified by binding to your configured LDAP/AD server with the user's password (TLS with certificate validation required unless allow_insecure is set); sessions are stateless HMAC tokens (12h access / 30d refresh by default) signed with QUBIT_DASHBOARD_LDAP_SECRET or a random per-process key, and logout cannot revoke them; group removal and disabled accounts are not re-checked until the refresh token expires; failed logins count toward the directory's account-lockout policy.

entries.name: dashboard-button
entries.description: One-click access to the Hermes Web Dashboard (127.0.0.1:9119) from the Desktop app — sidebar row, in-app page that loads itself when the server comes up, and a status-bar chip with a live dot. Front-end only: no agent calls, no tokens, no API keys.

entries.name: dashscope-image
entries.description: DashScope (Qwen Cloud) image generation -- Wan 2.7 models via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. Works with token plan (sk-sp-*) and PAYG (sk-ws-*) keys.

entries.name: dashscope-video
entries.description: DashScope (Qwen Cloud) video generation -- HappyHorse 1.1 models via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. Async task API. Works with token plan (sk-sp-*) keys.

entries.name: davinci-resolve
entries.description: Control DaVinci Resolve Studio live, or generate importable interchange files for free DaVinci Resolve.

entries.name: debug-desk
entries.description: Today's git digest in the current repo, plus the last failed terminal command the Qubit agent ran. Desktop pane, status chip, optional local LLM summary. Does not watch OS or editor terminals.

entries.name: deepgram-voice
entries.description: Deepgram Aura text-to-speech and Nova speech-to-text providers for Qubit Agent.

entries.name: deepinfra-sandbox
entries.description: Terminal backend running agent commands in isolated DeepInfra cloud sandboxes (deep_sands microVMs). Disclosure — runs agent commands in billable DeepInfra cloud sandboxes and uploads your Hermes skills, cache and skill-registered credential files to the sandbox at /workspace/.qubit; dangerous-command approval is skipped inside the sandbox.

entries.name: deepseek-whale
entries.description: Live DeepSeek API peak/off-peak pricing whale for the Qubit desktop titlebar. Blue x0.5 off-peak, grey PEAK at full price, countdown on click, 30s repaint, no backend or API key.

entries.name: deja-memory
entries.description: Memory from the coding sessions already on this machine — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes and the other agents deja reads, including history from before it was installed. No model, no API key, no server. Disclosure — runs the separately installed, unpinned deja binary (brew install deja-vu) as a subprocess; deja reads Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes and other agents' local transcript files, keeps its index under ~/.cache/deja, and recalled text from those agents is injected into Hermes turns; nothing leaves the machine.

entries.name: desensitize
entries.description: Chinese-context desensitization for Hermes chats. Replaces PII and business-sensitive entities — person names, company names, addresses, file paths, and magnitude figures — with reversible placeholders before a message reaches the model, then restores them in the reply. Two layers: an optional local/OpenAI-compatible LLM for semantic entity judgment, plus a sub-millisecond regex fallback (phone, ID card, email, IP, path) that keeps the conversation working when the model is unavailable. Disclosure — the semantic layer sends the pre-redaction text to the configured LLM, because recognising a name requires seeing it: with the default provider=ollama that is the local Ollama host and nothing leaves the machine, but provider=openai without an explicit base_url falls back to https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1 (remote); set base_url, or stay on ollama, to keep it local. Also rewrites inbound user messages and outbound assistant replies, so transcript content differs from what you typed; placeholders are code-generated and may over-match (18-digit ID-card-shaped strings, names that collide with the public-entity allowlist); company names are matched greedily and a modifier such as 原北京某某有限公司 is absorbed into the placeholder; magnitude masking drops the numeric value and only fires on the configured trigger words, so a domain term absent from that list is left unmasked without warning; the placeholder mapping is held in memory only and never written to disk.

entries.name: deskrpg
entries.description: Qubit gateway integration for DeskRPG virtual offices, with profiles, kanban, cron, artifacts and NPC skill management. Install it through the DeskRPG setup wizard. Optional (off by default): when enabled by the operator, links the plugin into every profile so kanban workers and cron runs can save artifacts. Disclosure — NPC skill management runs qubit skills/curator commands as background subprocesses per profile and edits that profile's skills, config.yaml and memory files; creating new review-policy kanban cards needs a review-policy API that upstream Qubit does not ship (the README points at the author's hermes-agent fork for it), and that feature stays inert on upstream.

entries.name: dexio
entries.description: Dexio shared-wiki memory. Before each turn, the pages of your Dexio wiki that match the user's message; tools to search, read and write the pages your other agents and team also use. Nothing is captured automatically: no transcripts or turn logs. Standard library only; no background threads or local services. Disclosure — with DEXIO_API_KEY set, the first 300 characters of each user message go to the Dexio server (default app.dexio.wiki, or DEXIO_URL) as a search query, tool arguments and the agent's profile name go there on tool calls, and the model is prompted to write, overwrite and edit pages in a wiki shared with the user's team and other agents, without a confirmation step.

entries.name: diaktoros
entries.description: Unattended GitHub pull-request review between two Hermes agents: one pushes fixes, a different one reviews, rounds are capped in verdicts, a watchdog reports silent stalls, and the loop never merges. Disclosure — runs unattended Hermes agent turns inside bubblewrap (terminal and file tools, no network, no credentials); a host-side broker and the CLI write to GitHub (reviews, comments, labels, issues, repo webhooks, and opt-in fixer pushes, which may push CI fixes and merge commits of the base into a PR's own branch to resolve conflicts; it never merges a PR) with repo-scope PAT files you provide; edits Hermes's webhook_subscriptions.json directly and its watchdog re-adds this loop's routes while armed; writes gate scripts into the seat profiles' scripts/ folders and creates one hermes cron job (its migrate command replaces the old hermes-review-loop job and copies that plugin's settings); downloads PR archives from codeload.github.com, failed CI job logs from GitHub's log storage (redirected, without the token) and Rust crates from crates.io on the host; an opt-in observer feed posts loop notices to the chat you name; deletes its own state and closed-PR review dirs in roots you configure; on OAuth seats its host proxy may force Hermes token refreshes that rewrite ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.qwen and profile auth.json credentials, and on Claude subscription logins it identifies as Claude Code (Claude Code user-agent, x-app and OAuth beta headers). Nothing runs until you arm a loop. Linux only.

entries.name: diff-review
entries.description: Analyze git diffs for common code quality issues — debug prints, hardcoded secrets, bare except clauses, and unresolved TODOs.

entries.name: document-reader
entries.description: Profile-scoped document OCR for Qubit Desktop and HUD, with a guarded per-profile Windows service.

entries.name: done-bell
entries.description: Ring when a Qubit turn finishes so you can leave the window. OS notification, optional chime, and a busy/done chip. Optional "needs you" when approval is waiting. No API keys.

entries.name: drag-to-pin-session
entries.description: Pin or unpin sessions from their row with supported desktop SDK actions.

entries.name: eatwise
entries.description: Eatwise (外卖营养教练) — local-first Chinese dietary coach: deterministic meal nutrition reviews, personal daily energy/nutrient targets, and consented on-device profile and meal history through 9 MCP tools over a bundled open food database (TFND + USDA FNDDS). No network, no accounts, no payments; profile schema rejects name/phone/ID/medical fields by design. Engine pinned to an immutable git commit (cbc08f6) over npx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs Node.js 22.5+ on PATH. Disclosure — the engine's MCP tool descriptions and error messages are Chinese-only while the skills are English-first.

entries.name: echarts-in-chat
entries.description: Render a chart inline in the Hermes Desktop transcript: the model emits ::echarts{labels=... values=...} and the plugin mounts an interactive SVG chart (dataZoom slider, click-to-filter legend, resize-aware, 280-560px height clamp) in the plugin SDK's transcript-directive slot. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no stored credentials, no environment variables, no background processes, and nothing read or written outside the message it renders; the chart is drawn locally as inline SVG with no third-party libraries.
entries.title: ECharts in Chat

entries.name: entropicmem
entries.description: Durable local memory for Qubit agents: SQLite FTS5 facts with cited, explainable recall; a Markdown vault with knowledge-graph export and an interactive visual graph; and turn-prefetch context injection with reason tokens. Write policy auto-redacts high-confidence secrets at write time (other PII types are warn-only findings) and stored-content injection screening flags and warns on recall and prefetch payloads (flag-and-warn, fail-open by design, not a blocking filter). Includes a 34-command CLI, destructive-op gates with automatic backups, and an append-only audit log. Disclosure — all memory data (vault markdown, memory.db, index.db, backups) stays local under QUBIT_HOME/entropicmem/; a shared publish DB defaults to QUBIT_HOME/entropicmem-shared/. The CLI init command appends ENTROPICMEM_* settings to QUBIT_HOME/.env (append-only). Vector embeddings are off by default; only with embeddings_enabled: true (provider) or ENTROPICMEM_EMBEDDINGS=1 / query --semantic (CLI) and the optional sentence-transformers extra installed does first use download all-MiniLM-L6-v2 weights from huggingface.co; otherwise the provider has no network egress. The CLI ingest command fetches a user-supplied URL; CLI graph export writes to ./export in the cwd by default and its HTML loads D3/marked from d3js.org and cdn.jsdelivr.net when opened; CLI graph serve starts a loopback HTTP server. entropicmem_patch_core edits the plugin's own Core-memory markdown (Persona/User_Profile), not Hermes core, and is off by default.

entries.name: epistemic-harness
entries.description: Record a provisional claim or uncertainty before an evidence-gathering step, then link the actual observation to it.

entries.name: error-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of failed provider calls (rate limits, overloads, timeouts, context overflows): /errors shows how many attempts failed per model, provider or cause, how many Hermes could retry, and the most common HTTP status, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /errors recent lists the newest failures and how long ago each happened. Disclosure — writes failed-attempt metadata (ids, provider, model, HTTP status, Hermes's failure class, exception class name, timings; no error message, request or prompt text) to plugin-data/error-ledger/errors.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network

entries.name: evalroute
entries.description: Route a task to the right (model, reasoning effort) arm before you start. Classifies the task into a lane, prints a provenance-carrying route card, and installs per-model reasoning-effort defaults. Strong rules run locally; weak-signal classification calls the host LLM and consumes tokens. The separate harness and shim can make paid provider calls when explicitly run; no plugin-owned credentials. Disclosure — weak-signal task classification sends the task text to your active Hermes model via the host LLM facade (token cost). The model-callable tool, /route, /rate and observed /model and /reasoning commands append task text and command args to a local ledger at <QUBIT_HOME>/evalroute/labels.jsonl. "qubit evalroute install-routes" rewrites agent.reasoning_overrides in config.yaml when you run it. The bundled harness and Hermes shim are never run by the plugin. When run by hand they make paid provider calls, execute model-generated code on the host via shell checkers, and run qubit -z with approvals bypassed.

entries.name: excel_line
entries.description: Excel-backed hierarchical long-term memory tree (10-row cap per workbook, dynamic branching, leaf pointers). Classifier defaults to the host model; third-party keyless rotation is opt-in.

entries.name: file-tray
entries.description: Session file tray — paths the Qubit agent touched via read_file, write_file, or patch. Desktop pane and /files. No API keys.

entries.name: filebox
entries.description: Dual-panel commander file browser for Qubit Desktop — whitelist-guarded file CRUD, copy/move/symlink, media preview, multi-select, rename, and trash. No network I/O, no model tokens.

entries.name: financial-datasets
entries.description: Stock market data from Financial Datasets - financial statements, prices, SEC filings, insider and institutional ownership, KPIs, news, macro data, and a stock screener.

entries.description: Fluxer gateway adapter for Qubit Agent. Native Fluxer integration using Fluxer's bot REST API for outbound messages, Gateway WebSocket events for inbound dispatches, message edits, agent-requested reactions, pins, reply references, media delivery, and channel-directory enumeration. Component button

entries.name: foresee
entries.title: Foresee
entries.description: Let AI assistants shop for home and auto insurance: compare instant quotes across every carrier. Connects to the hosted Foresee MCP server (Streamable HTTP at agents.go-foresee.com), with three workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package (hosted MCP server plus three skills), no Python and nothing runs locally; the vendor is Foresee Insurance Services, LLC (go-foresee.com). Every quote request sends the profile the user gives in chat (ZIP, age or date of birth, vehicles, drivers, driving record, home details) to agents.go-foresee.com with no account or API key. The live_carrier_quotes tool additionally sends the user's identity (name, date of birth, street address, email, optionally phone and driver's licence number) and, after the user's in-chat consent recorded verbatim, Foresee's agents submit those details to the selected insurance carriers, who may run a soft credit-based insurance score pull and contact the user. Foresee does not take payment or bind policies.

entries.name: freight-reconciliation
entries.description: Payer-side freight reconciliation: import carrier bills and trip ledgers into a deterministic local core (SQLite, WAL, no cloud), re-calculate against contracted rates and produce evidence-linked difference lists for human review — 14 MCP tools over uvx stdio (engine pinned to the immutable commit e8cd259c, release v0.4.1), with 3 bilingual workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs uv on PATH. Never approves payments, sends messages or writes back to ERP/TMS; final confirmations route through a local admin page the model cannot reach. Disclosure — the optional freight-admin page listens on 127.0.0.1 and is where a human confirms mappings, rules, matches and exports; nothing leaves the machine.

entries.name: frihet
entries.description: Official Hermes Agent integration for Frihet — discoverability, setup, diagnostics, and operating guidance for the Frihet MCP. Zero duplicated tools; the canonical 158-operation Frihet surface stays in @frihet/mcp-server and the remote endpoint https://mcp.frihet.io/mcp. Disclosure — /frihet setup and /frihet doctor send an unauthenticated MCP initialize to mcp.frihet.io (or FRIHET_MCP_URL); /frihet doctor also makes one read-only list_invoices call through Hermes's MCP client once you grant plugins.entries.frihet.mcp_allowlist; reads ~/.hermes/config.yaml only to check that an mcp_servers.frihet block exists; the pre_tool_call hook prompts before Frihet MCP calls it classifies as irreversible or unknown, but reads and draft-first creates pass without a prompt unless the server sets trust: untrusted.

entries.name: fusion
entries.description: Multi-model fusion router for Qubit: detects the model fleet your harnesses (Qubit, Codex, Claude, Grok) actually have installed and builds a Frontier -> Middle Manager -> Frontier routing structure with pinned models and provenance from execution records. `qubit fusion teams|validate|plan|run|index|report|status`.

entries.name: gbrain-plugin
entries.description: Community (non-official) plugin wiring GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT) into Qubit as a local memory layer over MCP: /gbrain status command, desktop starter, and per-profile Postgres setup/update/maintenance scripts. Not affiliated with upstream. Disclosure — the plugin itself only adds a /gbrain status command and a Desktop pane; GBrain is installed by the user via scripts/setup.sh, which installs bun (curl|bash), an unpinned gbrain from GitHub HEAD, and provisions PostgreSQL with sudo.

entries.name: gbrain-retrieval-reflex
entries.description: pre_llm_call hook plugin, enabled with `qubit plugins enable`: injects ambient context from a GBrain instance before each turn (volunteer_context, then a hybrid-query fallback). Not a `memory.provider`. Silent no-op when GBrain is unreachable or no token is set. Disclosure — before each non-trivial turn the last six user and assistant messages (truncated) and the current message are sent with a GBRAIN_TOKEN bearer token to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp), and returned brain-page text is injected into the turn.

entries.name: gemini-live-bridge
entries.description: Realtime duplex voice chat with the Gemini Live API — a status-bar minibar for the Qubit desktop app (transcript, model catalog, thinking level, session token meter, auto-redial via session resumption). Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live WebSocket and the user's key (requires_env GOOGLE_API_KEY); the desktop UI only talks to localhost and receives single-use ephemeral tokens. No agent tools; desktop-focused, dashboard tab hidden. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GOOGLE_API_KEY (or GEMINI_API_KEY) from the environment; input/output transcripts are held in backend memory for the session, and a Gemini session-resumption handle is written to .resume.json inside the plugin's install directory.

entries.name: gh-ref
entries.description: @gh:owner/repo#123 context references: attach a public GitHub issue or pull request to a message (title, state, labels, description, the latest comments; for pull requests also the branches, merge state and change size). Disclosure — sends anonymous HTTPS GET requests to api.github.com only (the referenced owner/repo and number leave the machine; no token, public repositories only, 60 requests an hour per IP address); no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @gh: reference provider.

entries.name: gigamail
entries.description: Email and calendar through an existing local GigaMail MCP server, with a workflow skill and stdio launcher. Requires Python and a separately configured backend; no automatic backend installation or updates. Reads real mail and attachments; sending, deletion and calendar writes use GigaMail's out-of-band human approval. Disclosure — a thin stdio launcher for the separately installed GigaMail MCP server from Adecubed inc. (gigamail.ai, github.com/adecubed/gigamail, same author as this plugin); the plugin holds no mail logic or credentials and downloads nothing, but it starts that third-party executable from PATH or a configured path, points it at GigaMail's own data directory under your user profile (%APPDATA%\ADE or ~/.ade), and send, delete and calendar writes are gated by that backend's out-of-band approval rather than by Hermes.

entries.name: git-hook
entries.description: Auto fetch/pull before reads, and commit + push only the files each turn changed, for every git worktree Hermes touches. Disclosure — after each turn it commits and pushes (push on by default; GIT_HOOK_PUSH=0 keeps commits local) the changed files of git worktrees under GIT_HOOK_ROOTS (default PROJECTS_ROOT, "*" for every repo), pushing to origin HEAD when no upstream is set; it pulls --ff-only before reads.

entries.name: githermes
entries.description: GitHub PRs and issues as a right workspace pane in Hermes Desktop, via the connected gh CLI. Disclosure — shells out to your logged-in gh CLI; the in-pane update pill only runs `qubit plugins update githermes` (no fetch-and-replace) and currently compares against upstream main rather than the pinned sha.

entries.name: github_app
entries.description: GitHub and GitHub Enterprise tools with bot-first attribution and approval-gated issue/PR writes. Disclosure — authenticates as a GitHub App from GITHUB_APP_ID, GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID and a private key in GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY or GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH/_FILE (read from the profile env or QUBIT_HOME/.env, held in memory only, never written or logged), falling back to GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN or `gh auth token` when no App variables are set, and reports which identity acted in every result. Talks only to https://api.github.com or the operator-configured GITHUB_API_URL / settings.api_url (HTTPS, no redirects; no tool argument can change the host). Issue/comment/review/merge writes stay disabled until settings.allow_write_actions is true and each one additionally goes through Hermes's human-approval prompt via its pre_tool_call hook (an 'always' answer does not persist).

entries.name: glasser
entries.description: Glasser's hosted MCP: search, inspect and run 1,000+ paid data endpoints (people and company enrichment, SEO, web, social media, US property, stock quotes) with one key, pay per call. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: a stdio bridge through mcp-remote (browser sign-in, no key in the package) plus a bundled skill for setup and the spending rules. Requires Node.js 18+. Disclosure — paid data broker: each run tool call charges your Glasser balance per the endpoint's published price with no in-Qubit confirm step; runs npx mcp-remote@0.14.3 as a local stdio bridge to https://api.glasser.ai/mcp; the sign-in token is cached by mcp-remote under ~/.mcp-auth/.

entries.name: gmail
entries.title: Gmail
entries.description: Hermes Desktop Gmail mailbox UI for search, reading, and thread inspection, with preview-confirmed send, reply, archive, trash, and label changes. Uses the active profile's existing Google Workspace OAuth setup; email is sensitive external content. Gmail actions and data access require user review and configuration. Disclosure — reads the active profile's Hermes Google Workspace token (google_token.json, refreshed in memory only) and calls the Gmail API; opening an unread message marks it read, other send/trash/label changes go through a confirm step (trash confirm can be turned off); remote email images load only after the user allows them.

entries.name: go-whatsapp
entries.title: Go WhatsApp
entries.description: Outbound WhatsApp tools through GOWA: registers GOWA's native MCP server and adds device listing, pairing, and removal. Setup can connect an existing server or explicitly install pinned GOWA v9.5.0 as a loopback-only authenticated native user service on Linux x86_64, macOS x86_64/arm64, or Windows x86_64. Disclosure — agents can send messages and mutate WhatsApp state through the linked account; session databases grant account access. The plugin does not ingest incoming messages or configure webhooks.

entries.name: gods-eye-view
entries.description: Explore God's Eye View inside Hermes Desktop, with the native 3D globe, scenes, Focus mode and explicit local engine controls. Disclosure — wraps the separate third-party God's Eye View app (installed by the user), starts/stops its local Node server on loopback and on explicit request updates that checkout from GitHub/npm (runs its esbuild install script); on explicit opt-in copies matching Hermes API keys into that app's own key store.

entries.name: gonogo
entries.description: Turn a pilot-scale eval score into a deployment decision — Wilson intervals, a confidence threshold that routes uncertain cases to a human, and an honest INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE verdict when the sample cannot support the claim.

entries.name: good-student
entries.description: Wrong-question diagnosis and study-action loop for parents and students — deterministic local core (SQLite, no cloud), host-model recognition gated by parent confirmation. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); good-student MCP server pinned to immutable commit 2469cbb over uvx, with the good-student workflow skill bundled. Needs Python 3.10+ via uv. No credentials required; all data stays on-device and nothing is uploaded.

entries.name: govee
entries.description: Discover and control Govee lights (power, brightness, color, white temperature, scenes) through Govee's developer API. Every command is checked against the model's advertised capabilities and ranges, then confirmed by a state read-back. Disclosure — sends device IDs and control commands to openapi.api.govee.com with your Govee API key; the model can change light state; stores nothing on disk.

entries.name: grill-tab
entries.description: Press Tab in the Desktop composer to grill a draft before it becomes a session: a fast auxiliary model asks one high-leverage decision at a time (with a recommended answer), then Enter synthesizes a faithful execution brief into the composer for review. Works for research, writing, planning, ops, design, and code; never auto-sends.

entries.name: grok-acp
entries.description: xAI Grok subscription as a Qubit model provider, driven over ACP stdio. Disclosure — spawns the vendor grok CLI found on PATH (grok agent over ACP stdio, plus grok models / grok login during setup) and drives your existing Grok subscription login; no API key is stored and Qubit provider secrets are stripped from the child environment.

entries.name: groq-provider
entries.description: Groq as a Hermes model provider (`--provider groq`, or Groq in `qubit model`): reasoning effort is sent in the form each Groq model accepts, so gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b work (through a custom endpoint, Hermes 0.21.5 sends them a value Groq rejects with HTTP 400), and the model list leaves out Groq's speech-to-text, text-to-speech, prompt-guard and 4K-context models that Hermes cannot run. Not affiliated with Groq. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 (or the configured model.base_url) through Hermes' own client with GROQ_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: ha-sidebar-navigator
entries.description: Full-power sidebar navigator & uncapped project/session explorer for Qubit Desktop. Bypasses the 3-session overview cap with searchable, scrollable project trees and timeline view.

entries.name: hades-coding-workflows
entries.description: Coding workflow skills — dual-model harness, subagent-driven development, and implementation planning patterns for Qubit Agent

entries.name: handflow
entries.description: Manus-style planning flow — the agent plans in steps and marks them as it works, with a live desktop pane.

entries.name: health-data
entries.description: Local health and daily-context data store for Qubit.

entries.name: health-insights
entries.description: Deterministic, local-first analysis of your own Apple Health data - weekly trends, rule-based concern checks, nutrition versus Dietary Reference Intakes, an IOM energy target, lab results and opt-in modules (GLP-1 monitoring, medication adherence; all off by default). entries.name: hicortex
entries.description: Shared fleet memory for Hermes agents: every connected agent learns from all other agents connected to the memory, wherever they run. Sessions across machines and harnesses are distilled into one common brain overnight — what one learns, the whole fleet recalls. Pushes a compact per-turn recall index (entries lazy-load via hicortex_get), injects fresh lessons plus a per-agent standing context block at session start — lesson blocks are delimited and carry an explicit reference-data framing line and provenance header — and exposes the full 9-tool memory surface (search, get, recent, ingest, lessons, index, graph, update, delete) through the shared server. The same server also serves Claude Code, OpenClaw, Pi and opencode agents, so mixed-harness fleets share one brain. Stdlib-only, no pip dependencies. Requires a running Hicortex server (npx @gamaze/hicortex init on any machine); data flow: each user message is sent to your configured Hicortex server for recall (default http://localhost:8787); session distillation runs on the server. Disclosure — sends every user message (and profile name) to your configured Hicortex server each turn for recall, default http://localhost:8787, plain http with a bearer token is accepted for remote servers with a one-time log warning; the server's standing Identity text and lessons are injected into the system prompt; the model can permanently update or delete shared fleet memories via hicortex_update / hicortex_delete without confirmation.

entries.name: hyatlas
entries.title: HyAtlas Memory
entries.description: HyAtlas v4 — self-hosted 7-layer memory provider backed by a pure-Go single-binary server you run yourself (chromem-go vectors, in-process BGE-small embeddings, bitemporal knowledge graph with source citations). Embeddings, the vector index and stored memories stay local. Ships agent tools (hyatlas_status/search/recent/add), a `hermes hyatlas` CLI, a Desktop pane with a starmap graph view, and a web dashboard. Disclosure — requires the separate hyatlas-go server, installed by the user. The plugin never downloads or bundles it, and it talks only to the configured server (default 127.0.0.1:19528). Embeddings and stored memories stay local. Extraction is opt-in: the server has no default LLM endpoint and makes no LLM call until HYATLAS_LLM_BASE, HYATLAS_LLM_MODEL and HYATLAS_LLM_KEY are all set. The repo installer pre-fills a free Nous Portal endpoint that Enter accepts, but nothing is sent until you also enter a key. Once configured, each turn, including that turn's tool output, goes to that endpoint. In the default ultra mode the server also sends batches of up to 200 stored facts to it every 6 hours and deletes the facts the model marks merged or stale. HYATLAS_MODE=lite makes no LLM call. The spawned server gets an allowlisted environment (OS essentials plus HYATLAS_*), not the agent's keys. auto_start is off by default. On Windows, if a hyatlas-go.ps1 launcher is configured or sits beside the binary, `hermes hyatlas start/stop` runs it; the repo's sample launcher reads your Nous token from Hermes auth.json and points extraction at the Nous Portal. No telemetry.
known_issues: After enabling, select the provider with `hermes memory setup` (memory.provider: hyatlas) — installing and enabling alone does not activate memory.
The agent tools and hooks arrive through the MemoryProvider interface, not ctx.register_tool, so they do not appear in the plugin tool list.
Requires the separate hyatlas-go server binary (installed by the user); without a reachable server the provider reports unavailable and memory features degrade rather than fail.

Thresholds in code, one JSONL line per decision with the fail-open reason, fail-open on every error path. Stdlib only, no Node; no redirects, proxy env ignored, payload capped; works with TYPESAFE_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY. Disclosure — each judged call sends the tool name and its redacted arguments (≤600 chars each, ≤12 args) to TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or your configured gateway, using your key; shadow mode only logs. With the default backend auto, OPENROUTER_API_KEY is used automatically whenever it is present and TYPESAFE_API_KEY is not, so tool names and redacted arguments go to openrouter.ai on your main-model OpenRouter key unless backend is set to typesafe or gateway.

entries.description: Names the one skill from your live roster that fits the turn, before the model call — typed routing via TypeSafe Jev (one choice over the roster plus gate booleans, then a re-read of the shortlist with per-candidate fits), with both thresholds applied in code. Says nothing when nothing fits; opt-in, fail-open, stdlib only, no Node; no redirects, proxy env ignored, payload capped. Disclosure — on eligible turns it sends your message (up to 4,000 chars) plus skill names and short SKILL.md excerpts from your local roster to TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or your configured gateway, using your key. With backend auto an OpenRouter key is used automatically when no TypeSafe key is set, and the OpenRouter route also reads Hermes' OpenRouter credential pool (auth.json) when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is absent, rotating that pool's entries through the core pool API.

entries.name: jev-typesafe
entries.description: TypeSafe Jev (System One) decision tools — atomic yes/no checks, routing, rubric scoring and mixed typed questions with calibrated probabilities, for triage, routing and review gating in coding agents. Disclosure — every tool call sends the model-supplied question/state together with your TYPESAFE_API_KEY to api.typesafe.ai (TypeSafe AI, an independent vendor); the catalog has not verified the plugin author's affiliation with that vendor.

entries.name: jev
entries.description: Explicit Jev decision sidekick via TypeSafe or Cloudflare; advisory judgments, no automatic tool gating.

entries.name: jira-browser
entries.description: Jira workspace for Hermes Desktop, linking tickets to Hermes Projects, worktrees, and conversations. Disclosure — reads a Jira API token from JIRA_* env vars or ~/jira-config/config.json (owner-only, read-only) and sends it only to your configured https Jira origin; agent tools are read-only but return Jira text (untrusted) to the model; Start work / Draft update create chats seeded with ticket descriptions (Draft update auto-runs a turn); PR/CI status is read through your local gh CLI login.

entries.name: job-search
entries.description: A private, local-first job-search assistant that finds postings, judges them against your prose preferences (no scores), and writes digests on a schedule you control.

entries.name: jot
entries.description: Notes, checklists and documents beside Hermes that your agent can read and update safely, with revision checks and undo for AI edits.
entries.title: Jot
known_issues: Requires a current Hermes Desktop build with SandboxedFrame and gateway file-download SDK support.
Word attachments use download or the default application; the tested host does not render DOCX.

entries.name: jp-charts
entries.description: Bar, line, stacked and 100% band charts as phone-sized PNGs for chat replies and reports, with Japanese text, 万/億 units and a required unit and source line. Every bar, point, label and tick is read back from the finished figure and compared with the parsed data before the image is returned. Disclosure: no network calls at run time; reads a local .csv/.tsv/.txt/.json only when given its path (never hidden files or the Hermes home); writes PNGs to the Hermes image cache; a transform_llm_output hook adds a forgotten MEDIA line to replies on chat platforms and cron deliveries (setting auto_attach, on by default).

entries.name: jp-corporate
entries.description: Japanese corporate lookup (法人照会): find or verify a company by name or corporate number and read its gBizINFO record (basic info, subsidies, government contracts, awards, certifications, financials, patents, workplace data). Disclosure — sends the company names, corporate numbers and prefectures you look up to api.info.gbiz.go.jp (METI gBizINFO) with your own GBIZINFO_API_TOKEN in a request header; no other host, nothing written to disk.

entries.name: jp-egov-law
entries.description: Japanese laws for Hermes Agent, built on the e-Gov Law API: find a law by name, abbreviation or phrase, read one article as in force today or on a given date, and check amendment history and enforcement dates, with the source credit e-Gov's terms ask for. Disclosure — sends the law names, article numbers, dates and search phrases you look up to laws.e-gov.go.jp (public API, no key); no other host, nothing written to disk.

entries.name: jp-estat
entries.description: Japanese government statistics for Hermes Agent, built on the e-Stat API (政府統計の総合窓口, Japan's official government statistics portal): search tables, see their categories, and fetch numbers by name (population, households, establishments by industry, wages, consumer prices) with units, survey dates and citations. Disclosure — sends your search words and table selections to api.e-stat.go.jp with your own ESTAT_APP_ID (e-Stat requires the ID in the request URL); no other host, nothing written to disk.

entries.name: junie-acp
entries.description: JetBrains Junie coding agent as a Qubit model provider over ACP.

entries.name: kanban-gantt
entries.description: Gantt timeline view for the Qubit kanban boards: a full /kanban-gantt desktop page rendering any board as a timeline of real work timestamps (created/started/review/done), with dependency tree connectors, live-activity arcs, filters, bulk actions, and a dockable task detail drawer. Zero API keys, zero model tokens.

entries.name: kanban-live-gantt
entries.description: Live, now-centered Gantt timeline for the Hermes kanban boards — a slidable, persisted 72 h window (default now -24h -> now +48h; drag to move, drag the ends to resize), free wheel zoom down to hour ticks, a now line, status filtering, an optional done lane, and lifecycle rendering (dashed waiting vs solid run spans at real durations). Fork of kanban-gantt (GPL-3.0). Disclosure — the backend can transition, reassign, comment on and permanently delete kanban tasks on any board (Desktop asks for confirmation before deletes); local SQLite only, no network.

entries.name: kanban-task-threads
entries.description: Give every Qubit kanban task a live Discord forum thread with a rewritten status card and append-only event log. Disclosure — sends task and lifecycle data to the configured Discord webhook (no host allowlist). Cards and event replies use built-in or operator-configured templates and may include identifiers, titles, status, assignment, branch and workspace metadata, relationships and blocking details, comments, event actors, reviewers, reasons, summaries, and configured dashboard links; the comment excerpt length is configurable. Fixed prerequisite announcements additionally send the prerequisite task ID, title, assignee, and up to 140 characters of its body and are not template-configurable. The absolute workspace path is off by default and requires explicit opt-in. Reads the kanban database read-only and stores thread mapping state under <kanban_home>/kanban/plugins/kanban-task-threads/. With an optional existing publisher-profile Discord bot token, reads forum and thread metadata; creates or repairs managed status tags and emojis; replaces applied tags on plugin-managed threads; renames threads; and archives or unarchives them. Discord fetches webhook avatars from the configured HTTPS asset origin. Disclosure — the avatar asset origin defaults to the author-hosted https://diegomarino.github.io/kanban-task-threads (disable with avatars_enabled: false). With the bot token the periodic metadata audit also lists the guild's active threads (filtered to the forum) and may rewrite the forum's available-tag list to add the 11 managed status tags (requires Manage Channels).

entries.name: kimi-code-delegate
entries.description: Delegate-only, fail-closed Kimi Code ACP integration for Qubit Agent

entries.name: kiro-acp
entries.description: Kiro CLI (AWS) as a Qubit model provider, driven over ACP stdio.

entries.name: kiro-provider
entries.description: Native Kiro model provider over HTTPS with AWS Builder ID / IAM Identity Center device login. Disclosure — dynamically registers an AWS OIDC public client named `hermes-kiro` during login and stores OAuth grants in Qubit' profile-scoped auth.json credential pool.

entries.name: kiwi
entries.description: Source suppliers and negotiate purchases through the Kiwi Buyer MCP server — an open-source A2A commerce runtime (pinned @harrylabsj/kiwi@0.11.0 over npx stdio), with the kiwi-buyer sourcing workflow skill bundled. Sourcing is dual-source: Kiwi Network results come from kiwi_search, and internet e-commerce listings are reported through the host's own web tools when the session has them (a host capability, not a plugin guarantee). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js/npm on PATH. No credentials required; Kiwi never handles payments.

entries.name: kuma
entries.description: Uptime-Kuma monitoring for agents: the community MCP server for Uptime Kuma v2 (pinned @0.11.18 over npx stdio) with workflow skills for incident review, status digests, and confirmation-gated maintenance. Credentials stay in host-native MCP config (portable Agent Plugins v1 package, mcp.json + skills/; needs Node.js >= 22 on PATH and a Uptime Kuma v2 instance). Disclosure — first run has npx fetch @davidfuchs/mcp-uptime-kuma@0.11.18 (single-maintainer community package) from npm; that server exposes 31 read/WRITE tools against your Uptime Kuma instance, including permanent delete tools the bundled skills never call.

entries.name: lancedb-suite
entries.description: Local-first LanceDB vector memory with a strict write contract, calibrated abstention, typed relations, conflict tracking and a retrieval-quality gate. Requires local Ollama + nomic-embed-text.

entries.name: lancedb
entries.description: LanceDB hybrid memory — embedded vector + FTS recall, workspace facts, transparent forget.

entries.name: letsfg
entries.title: LetsFG
entries.description: Search and book real flights and hotels through the hosted LetsFG MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR), with the letsfg travel-booking workflow skill bundled: fares across airlines and the major travel sites, flexible dates, destinations in a region, bookable hotel rates, then book, follow and stop bookings. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at letsfg.co/mcp. Booking tools act on real money: a booking holds the price on the card saved on the user's LetsFG account (captured only once the airline or hotel confirms, released if it fails), is approved from an e-mail by default, and card details are only ever entered on letsfg.co, never in the conversation. Traveller details given for a booking (name, date of birth, passport, contact) are sent to LetsFG and saved on that account. OAuth must be enabled with `qubit mcp add letsfg --url https://letsfg.co/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: lib-docs
entries.description: Look up current library docs from public npm and PyPI (no API keys). Resolve a package, fetch README and metadata, keep recent lookups on Desktop. Disclosure — HTTPS to registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org and cdn.jsdelivr.net (npm READMEs) only; package name and version leave the machine; recent lookups are stored under $QUBIT_HOME/plugin-data/lib-docs; the Desktop pane inserts text through Qubit Desktop's internal qubit:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API).

entries.name: limbic
entries.description: Self-organising memory provider (MemoryProvider ABC): local SQLite (WAL) with sqlite-vec KNN + FTS5 hybrid recall, adaptive trust scoring, activation maturation, interference-based forgetting, NLI-based correction detection and synaptic atrophy. No LLM cost — all lifecycle mechanisms are deterministic. Tools (remember/recall) and lifecycle hooks dispatch via the MemoryManager from the registered provider — this entry registers a MemoryProvider only, so provides_tools/provides_hooks are empty. Disclosure — on first use downloads ~1.0GB of ONNX models (Arctic Embed 2.0 L int8 embedding, ~570MB; MiniLMv2 NLI, ~430MB) from huggingface.co at pinned commits with hash checks into ~/.cache/limbic/ (outside HERMES_HOME; an older fp32 cache of ~2.2GB is left in place); spaCy NER models are not downloaded and must be installed manually for entity extraction; memory stays local in limbic.db under HERMES_HOME, and hermes backup adds VACUUM snapshots under HERMES_HOME/backups; no telemetry. Stores created or reindexed on 0.6.0+ record the embedder that produced their vectors and report stale_embedder=true after an embedder change until `hermes limbic reindex`; stores from 0.5.x keep serving their fp32 vectors unflagged until reindexed. PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (commercial use requires a separate license).

entries.name: linkup
entries.description: Linkup web search: live cited search (fast/standard/deep), URL-to-Markdown fetch with JS rendering, async deep research, and a Linkup backend for the built-in web_search / web_extract tools. Disclosure — sends search queries, fetch URLs and research briefs to api.linkup.so with your LINKUP_API_KEY (Linkup fetches pages server-side); when selected with qubit linkup use-as-web-backend it also handles the built-in web_search and web_extract calls; large fetched pages are cached under $QUBIT_HOME/cache/linkup for 24 hours.

entries.name: little-canary
entries.description: Screens user turns and blocks downstream tools on a BLOCK verdict; the original prompt still reaches the model.
entries.maintainer: roli-lpci (Hermes Labs; independent of Nous Research)

entries.name: live-time
entries.description: Inject live current time into every LLM call via the pre_llm_call hook — fixes stale session-start timestamps in long/cross-day conversations.

entries.name: local-system-one-qubit
entries.title: Local System One
entries.description: Local System One / Laya Typed Decisions control plane for Hermes Agent. Sends task text to a loopback sidecar for reversible OFF/Shadow/Canary routing decisions, with explicit Canary acknowledgement and fail-open behavior. Disclosure — executes nothing and does not start the sidecar. In Shadow/Canary mode it POSTs each turn's task text (last user message up to 4000 chars, or the owned Kanban card title/body) plus up to 2000 chars of recent user/assistant messages to the configured sidecar URL (default loopback 127.0.0.1:8787; user-configurable to any host; no auth header). Its only request mutations, in acknowledged Canary mode on the first provider call of a turn, are removing the web_search/web_extract tools and (off by default) lowering reasoning_effort for gemini-3.8-flash-tiered; plugin state is metadata-only under plugin-data/. The sidecar (same repo, separate pip install, Apple-Silicon MLX/CoreML) is a text classifier that downloads a pinned Hugging Face model.

entries.name: local_knowledge
entries.description: Native Qubit tools for a configurable local capability index: search/get/neighbors plus local usage feedback/reporting.

entries.name: localsend
entries.description: Peer-to-peer file transfer over the LocalSend protocol - discover the phones, laptops and tablets on your LAN, send files to them, and run a headless receiver so they can send files back. Ships a desktop pane, a status-bar chip and three palette commands, and speaks LocalSend's default encrypted mode. Standard library only, no accounts, no cloud.

entries.name: lumberroom
entries.description: lumberroom memory provider. One durable store shared with every agent you use, recalled on every turn and written through the engine's own memory_write. Self-hosted open-source engine or lumberroom.cloud; OAuth or a static token. Maintained by the lumberroom team. Disclosure — when active, every non-trivial user message (first 1,000 characters) and the absolute git-root path of the working directory are sent on each turn to the configured lumberroom engine, which defaults to https://mcp.lumberroom.cloud (operated by Cybersapien Technologies, India) unless base_url names a self-hosted engine; the model is instructed to store decisions, preferences and facts there through memory_write, the engine's live tool descriptions and server instructions are injected into the system prompt each session, and setup switches off Hermes' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md store.

entries.name: made-shelf
entries.description: Everything Hermes made - cross-session shelf of wrote/patched paths. Full Desktop page, chip, pin. No API keys.

entries.name: markdown-new
entries.description: Search the public web, read pages as Markdown, crawl sites, and convert documents in Hermes. No API key required. Disclosure — search queries, submitted URLs and explicitly approved local file uploads go to the public markdown.new service; needs the companion markdown-new CLI (uv tool install from the same repo tag), which the plugin runs as a subprocess with the Hermes process environment.

entries.name: markifact
entries.description: Run Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, GA4, Shopify, HubSpot and 50+ more platforms through Markifact's hosted MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with ten skills (operating protocol, write-safety rules, campaign launch, creative rotation, negative sweeps, diagnosis); remote streamable-http with OAuth 2.1 and dynamic client registration, so no Node.js or API keys. Disclosure: creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets; every write is a separate approval-gated operation and the skills instruct confirm-before-spend, but that is enforced by the skills and the server's approval flag, not by Qubit.

entries.name: meeting-overlay
entries.description: Disclosure — sends meeting transcripts to Qubit inference with your Qubit login (fallback OpenRouter key from ~/.hermes/.env; optional OCTOPUS_DESK_URL); installs a launchd agent that records mic/system audio; writes and deletes under your Obsidian vault; macOS + source install only. Native desktop pane showing the live meeting transcript, answer, and daemon status.

entries.name: mem-os
entries.description: Local-first persistent memory: store durable facts once and recall them in any session. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): the @mem-os/sdk MCP server (pinned 1.6.26) over npx stdio, plus the mem-os-memory skill covering when to store and when to recall. All data stays in a local SQLite database under the user home directory; no cloud, no telemetry, no API keys. Server cwd is ${PLUGIN_DATA} so nothing is written into the install tree. Needs Node.js and npm on PATH.

entries.name: memanto
entries.description: Memanto memory agent — typed long-term memory (remember/recall/answer) with auto-recall, turn capture, and RAG answers. Disclosure — each user turn (as a recall query), completed user+assistant turns, Hermes memory writes and memanto_answer questions are sent to Moorcheh cloud (api.moorcheh.ai) under a per-profile agent namespace by default; requires MOORCHEH_API_KEY; settings in $QUBIT_HOME/memanto.json.

entries.name: memex8
entries.description: Self-hosted vector memory (Qdrant + TurboQuant compression) with auto-discovered knowledge realms, semantic search across conversations and ingested documents, and a slumber pipeline for memory consolidation. v1.1.0 adds optional per-session injection dedup with char-budget gate, decision/evaluation memory-type promotion (slower decay for load-bearing turns), prompt-injection sanitization on read, configurable system-prompt template, export/import memories as JSON, and a /memex8 slash command. New memory behaviours are opt-in; /memex8 export|import is confined to $QUBIT_HOME/plugin-data/memex8 unless enable_export_import=true. Disclosure — auto-stores a truncated copy (first 300 chars) of every user and assistant turn, plus per-message previews of the whole transcript at session end and before context compression, to the memex8 server at MEMEX8_BASE_URL (self-hosted; default http://localhost:8080) using MEMEX8_API_KEY.

entries.name: memlock
entries.description: Reasserts pinned standing instructions after context compaction. Disclosure — scope=global pins apply to every session sharing the same QUBIT_HOME; memlock_setup.py edits config.yaml and .claude/settings.json (with backups) only when you run it.

entries.name: memobase
entries.description: Memobase memory provider — self-hosted user profile + event timeline recall, with hybrid BM25/vector/entity retrieval and automatic per-turn prefetch.

entries.name: memory-review
entries.description: Checkbox staged memory writes and approve or reject the selection from a dialog.

entries.name: memory-rewind
entries.description: Automatic version history for the built-in memory (MEMORY.md, USER.md), SOUL.md and skills/ (including curator-archived skills): browse, diff and restore any past version with `qubit memory-rewind`, or view it from any chat with the read-only `/memory-history`. Works alongside the built-in memory; not a memory provider. Disclosure — runs the local git binary (isolated from the user's git config, hooks and signing) to keep a bare repository in $QUBIT_HOME/plugin-data/memory-rewind/; reads only the tracked files (never .env, auth.json, databases or skills/.hub/); rewrites tracked files only when the user runs `restore`; no network.

entries.name: memory-zvec
entries.description: Community Zvec memory backend for Qubit Agent - in-process HNSW + RocksDB FTS store with native hybrid retrieval and session-safe lock governance; embeddings via any Ollama-compatible endpoint (local Ollama bge-m3 by default).

entries.name: memtomem
entries.description: Markdown-first long-term memory shared across your coding agents: a local memtomem MCP server plus six memory skills (index, recall, remember, search, setup, status). Notes live in ~/.memtomem and are searchable from Hermes, Claude Code, Codex CLI and Kimi Code. Runs at user scope. Disclosure — the server is launched with `uvx --python 3.12` and downloaded from PyPI (memtomem[onnx]==0.6.6) on first start, with Python 3.12 if uv cannot find one; it runs as a stdio MCP server for the session and reads the directories you ask it to index. With a fresh BM25-only configuration nothing else leaves the machine; an existing memtomem configuration may enable Hugging Face model downloads, a remote embedding or LLM provider, Cohere reranking or search webhooks.

entries.name: mermail
entries.description: Privacy-first agent email inboxes and workspace automation through hosted Mermail MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/, seventeen skills bundled); authenticate with OAuth via `qubit mcp login mermail`. No credentials are stored in mcp.json. Disclosure — the bundled skills also expose Mermail's paybox wallet tools over the hosted MCP (x402 payments, xStocks trading, standing grants); the skills allow the agent to move funds without a same-turn confirmation when your message already states exact terms, so spending controls live on your Mermail account, not in Qubit.

entries.name: metamask-wallet
entries.description: MetaMask Agent Wallet for Qubit — chat-only setup, reads, and approval-gated transfers/swaps/signatures, a gated Guard Mode policy editor, and a background 2FA watcher. Keys stay in MetaMask.

entries.name: metronix
entries.description: Metronix memory provider for Qubit with prefetch recall and built-in memory write-through.

entries.name: microsoft365
entries.description: Pre-release Microsoft 365 Graph tools for Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive, Calendar, Teams, To Do, and Planner.

entries.name: mindgraph
entries.description: MindGraph — semantic graph memory with hybrid retrieval, goal/decision tracking, and cross-document synthesis.

entries.name: minecraft-platform
entries.description: Minecraft gateway adapter for Qubit Agent. Spawns a Mineflayer bot that joins a Minecraft server, wanders around, and relays chat messages between players and the Qubit agent. Supports offline and Microsoft-authenticated accounts.

entries.name: minimax-image
entries.description: MiniMax image generation -- Image-01 models via MiniMax platform. Supports text-to-image and image-to-image with subject reference.

entries.name: minimax-search
entries.description: MiniMax web search via the Token Plan API — keyed, no CAPTCHA

entries.name: minimax-video
entries.description: MiniMax (Hailuo) video generation -- Hailuo 2.3/02 and S2V-01 models via MiniMax platform. Async task API. Supports text-to-video, image-to-video, and subject-reference-to-video.

entries.name: mnemostack
entries.description: Persistent agent memory over a mnemostack service or a local Qdrant — hybrid recall (vector + lexical + graph), verbatim capture with self-echo suppression, and soft retraction. Multi-tenant when pointed at a shared authenticated service; the tenant is resolved server-side from the service key. Disclosure — the pinned directory is a discovery shim; the provider code installs from PyPI at the version pinned in plugin.yaml pip_dependencies (qubit-mnemostack==1.0.3) into the Hermes venv. Configured via MNEMOSTACK_* env vars; no key is required for a purely local Qdrant setup.

entries.name: mnemosyne-dashboard
entries.description: Local-only web dashboard for browsing and visualising Mnemosyne memories, triples, stats, and consolidation history.

entries.name: mnemosyne
entries.description: Local-first memory layer for Qubit Agent — SQLite with vector + FTS5 hybrid recall, episodic consolidation, temporal knowledge graph. Zero cloud. Disclosure — the mnemosyne_remember_media tool refuses local file paths unless MNEMOSYNE_MEDIA_ALLOWED_PATHS is set and sends media only to an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint when modality_enabled is on; video uses ffmpeg/ffprobe from PATH; the embedding model (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) downloads from Hugging Face on first use.

entries.name: model-usage-status
entries.description: Provider-native Claude and Codex remaining allowance windows in the Qubit Desktop status bar. Disclosure — spawns the local `codex app-server` and `claude auth status` CLIs and reads the Claude OAuth token read-only through Qubit core; the optional install.sh (not part of the catalog install) edits the statusLine in ~/.claude/settings.json; macOS only.

entries.name: morning-briefing
entries.description: Personal daily newspaper for Qubit: gathers weather, calendar, AQI, curated 36-hour news (timestamped Reddit RSS + X + web search, per-story QR codes), and newsletter digests, renders one 8.5x11 newsprint page, and prints it every morning via a cron job.

entries.name: mrscraper
entries.description: MrScraper web search, rendered extraction, crawling, and scraper tools. Disclosure — every tool call is a paid MrScraper API request billed to your account; URLs, prompts and schemas you pass are sent to mrscraper.com.

entries.name: my-github
entries.description: Desktop and dashboard plugin: statusbar chip, palette command, and dashboard tab listing your GitHub repos (public + private) via the gh CLI.

entries.name: mybot-farm
entries.description: Search mybot.farm, plant/reinstall Qubit packs (Desktop Recruit + CLI), and post GAF listings. Disclosure — plants third-party Qubit profiles (config, SOUL, skills, memories) from mybot.farm sellers with no hash pinning; force/clean delete profiles.

entries.name: nachos
entries.description: Durable memory and context compression for Hermes Agent with local SQLite or flat-file storage. Disclosure — replaces the memory provider (memory.provider: nachos) and, only when context.engine: nachos is set, the context engine; the provider injects a system-prompt block telling the agent to use the nachos_memory_* tools and keep built-in memory disabled; opt-in semantic ranking either runs a separately installed nachos-embeddings CLI or sends the turn query plus memory titles/summaries to api.openai.com with OPENAI_API_KEY; all storage is local under /nachos/.

entries.name: needs-you
entries.description: Qubit is waiting — full Desktop page for pending approvals. Queue, chip, OS notify. Redacted previews only. No API keys.

entries.name: nerve
entries.description: Nerve is a supervisory nervous system for Qubit Agent with provider-neutral Jev, Laya, and OpenJev Reflex backends, evidence-backed Kanban supervision, context governance, token-budget trajectory control, and durable SSH workers. Disclosure — the default Reflex backend is hosted Jev; with the default settings (enabled / admission_enabled on) each turn's user prompt (up to 12k characters) and redacted tool/result previews are sent to the configured Jev provider (OpenRouter Decisions / TypeSafe Jev) using your OPENROUTER_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_API_KEY, spending your credits on every turn. Laya and OpenJev can be configured as local/self-hosted backends. The operator-only nerve setup CLI can copy a local QubitContextBus checkout into QUBIT_HOME/plugins/qubit-context-bus and runs qubit plugins enable/disable for that plugin when a profile is saved; the model cannot trigger this.

entries.name: next-prompt
entries.description: Suggests your next message after each turn as a pill under the Desktop composer: your likely answer when the agent asks you something, or the natural next step.

entries.name: nextdns
entries.description: Read-only NextDNS tools - DNS query logs, blocked queries with the blocklist that matched, and aggregate analytics by domain, device, blocklist or protocol. For triaging DNS problems and answering "was this blocked, and by what". Uses the official NextDNS API; makes no configuration changes.

entries.name: node-search
entries.description: Bounded Markdown metadata+graph prefilter for configured local roots

entries.name: ntfy-approval
entries.description: Answer Hermes' approval prompts from your phone: once selected with security.approval.transport: ntfy, each dangerous-command prompt arrives as an ntfy push notification with Approve once, Approve for session and Deny buttons, and no answer still means deny. Disclosure — once selected, anyone who can read the ntfy topic can approve dangerous commands (the one-time answer codes are in the notification), so on the public ntfy.sh default the topic name is the only secret and NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN is optional; each pending approval publishes Hermes' reason, the redacted command (unless send_command is false), the non-default profile name and one-time answer codes to the configured ntfy server, then reads <topic>-reply and deletes the notification; any failure or timeout is a deny; reads NTFY_APPROVAL_TOPIC/NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN from the profile .env, never puts the token in a notification, follows no redirects, writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: nvidia-app
entries.description: NVIDIA App control through its local MCP server: overlay capture and state, driver status and release notes, game optimization, and app launch. Requires NVIDIA App 11.0 or newer on Windows; the install is refused when the app is absent, and the tools appear while the app's service is running. The plugin reads the endpoint and token NVIDIA App publishes in its own McpServer server.json on every connection, so a changed port or token needs no reconfiguration. Disclosure: the tools read and change NVIDIA App settings on this machine; nothing leaves loopback.
entries.title: NVIDIA App

entries.name: nvidia-broadcast
entries.description: NVIDIA Broadcast control through its local MCP gateway: camera, microphone and speaker effects, Studio Voice profiles, device selection, camera resolution, and effects on local media files. Requires NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 or newer on Windows (2.2 and older have no gateway); the install is refused when the app is absent, and the tools appear while NVIDIA Broadcast is running in the user's desktop session. entries.name: openltm
entries.description: Long-term memory for Hermes agents, stored in a local SQLite database. FTS5 full-text search with optional vector (sqlite-vec) recall, importance-weighted decay, a queryable memory graph, and automatic capture: a declarative rule engine classifies corrections, constraints, preferences, decisions, and agent-discovered facts from a conversation and stores each one as a distilled, self-contained fact. Runtime notifications and read-only OpenLTM tool requests are excluded by named guards so ops noise never becomes memory. No cloud, no telemetry, no API keys required; optional Gemini/OpenAI/Ollama providers for embeddings. MIT licensed.

entries.description: One install: the Desktop model picker and the OR Picker composer provider. Checking a model here is what the composer lists. Disclosure — the optional OpenRouter management key is stored in plaintext in Desktop localStorage; the plugin reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY from your environment, Hermes secret store or QUBIT_HOME/.env and sends it only to openrouter.ai (credits, usage, and the Test-model button, which spends credits).
