entries.name: optmem-qubit
entries.description: Independent Hermes integration of Victor Taelin's OptMem design: local, append-only memory with regex/BM25 recall and a bounded wake digest. Hybrid and guarded OptMem-only modes; verified migration and rollback. Local by default. Compaction is manual unless auto_nap is enabled. Optional LLM summaries run only when both auto_nap and llm_summary are on; they send memory blocks to the configured provider via host-owned authentication and may incur token costs. Summaries are lossy, raw records remain recoverable, and conflicts are not resolved automatically. Wake consumes model context. See README for upstream attribution. Disclosure — memory is stored locally under QUBIT_HOME; optional auto_nap+llm_summary sends stored memory lines to the user's configured model provider; the optmem-only mode (explicit CLI with --yes) disables Hermes' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md injection after a verified backup.

entries.name: orbit-desktop
entries.description: Your workspace, shaped by your agent: a bundled browser desktop powered by Hermes. Describe the workflow you need; the agent can rearrange windows and panes, customize appearance, build versioned sandboxed web apps, and refine your workspace with scoped control, previews and checkpoints. Illustrated examples show a project-specific COCS 3D asset viewer and OmniVoice experiment bench; these example apps and their backends are not bundled. Includes permission-controlled desktop agent-reply notifications (generic alerts while Orbit remains open; browser/OS restrictions apply) and 100,000-character chat messages, guidance and drafts. Includes Devplan Studio for guided interviews, specifications, phased devplans and circular-development handoff exports. Optional conversational interviews require explicit service setup and a working Hermes provider login, and send project context to that provider. Includes 14 distinctive interface presets including Nous Atelier, with local wallpapers, themed icons and taskbar treatments. Agent chats include inline expandable tool activity, running/completed/failed summaries, an activity strip, a workspace agent overview and responsive toolbar controls. Missing tool-call IDs are explicitly uncorrelated. Embedded apps retain their own styling. Includes a reviewed GitHub app catalog with immutable source pins and a portable Live Telemetry package. Catalog sync (operator-run scripts/orbit_catalog.py, never triggered by the Hermes tool or at register) reads the entry list from the upstream repo's main branch at sync time and downloads third-party static app bundles at their per-entry commit pins; installed UI runs in a sandboxed iframe and never executes backend code. Optional telemetry backend staging downloads pinned Python; execution requires explicit host-code trust and separate private authenticated HTTPS setup. Backend code runs with owner privileges, not a sandbox. Disclosure — adapter talks only to the configured local Orbit server (loopback, Bearer capability from runtime_dir); mutations off by default. Optional orbit.py setup runs npm ci / node. Bundled VNC/Xpra launchers use the Orbit page's hostname and scheme; optional Linux apps require separate provisioning. Optional api.typesafe.ai requests require explicit consent and a user-supplied key. The 0.2.7 web app's opt-in Show tools panel displays tool call arguments and results for the current Hermes conversation, fetched from the local Orbit server and local Hermes session API and kept in the browser only. The Nous Atelier theme contains Nous Research logo artwork and is unofficial; Orbit is not affiliated with Nous Research.

entries.name: orcaslicer
entries.title: OrcaSlicer for Hermes
entries.description: Prepare, slice, preflight and export 3D prints with stock OrcaSlicer profiles. Includes explicit printer upload/control, camera snapshots and monitoring through supported protocols. Protocol and hardware limits are documented. Independent of OrcaSlicer and Nous Research. Disclosure — executes the installed local slicer and exposes printer upload, start, pause, resume and cancel; agent-supplied confirmation is not independent human authentication. Printer/camera credentials are read from ORCA_*/QUBIT_ORCA_* environment variables named in tool arguments (HTTPS required unless allow_plaintext_credentials is set); plugin state lives in ~/.qubit-orca (QUBIT_ORCA_HOME), outside QUBIT_HOME.

entries.name: osv-ref
entries.description: @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: context references: attach a vulnerability record from OSV.dev to a message (summary, aliases, severity, affected packages with version ranges and fixed versions, details, references), with package data merged from up to four alias records. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/<id> only (the referenced id and up to four of its alias ids leave the machine); no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: reference providers.

entries.name: parallel-search
entries.description: Free web search and page fetching through Parallel's hosted MCP, with a setup skill bundled. No account or API key required. Queries and requested URLs are sent to Parallel. Adds direct MCP tools alongside Qubit's native web providers.

entries.name: parrotnotes
entries.description: Find, search, summarize and save insights for your ParrotNotes in-person meeting notes through the hosted ParrotNotes MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0 + DCR), with the parrotnotes workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.parrotnotes.app (OAuth via a Supabase auth backend); note titles, transcripts and insights from the user's ParrotNotes account are pulled into the session context, and text the model passes to save_note_insight is written to that account. OAuth must be enabled with `qubit mcp add parrotnotes --url https://mcp.parrotnotes.app/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: pcs-security-tls-posture
entries.description: Read-only audit of local TLS posture — certificate validity, key strength, deprecated protocols, weak cipher suites, and the certificate each server's configuration points at. Disclosure — reads a fixed list of system certificate and nginx/Apache config paths under / (or a caller-supplied prefix); makes no network connections and runs no subprocesses. If the sibling plugin pcs-security-core is installed, its copy of the shared contract is loaded in preference to the bundled one.

entries.name: pep-ref
entries.description: @pep:<number> context references: attach a Python Enhancement Proposal to a message (status, type, authors, Python version and its first section, usually the Abstract), or one section with @pep:<number>#<section>, with PEP number and title autocomplete in the TUI and Desktop composer. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to peps.python.org only (the PEP index and the referenced PEP's page; section names and autocomplete text are matched locally); keeps the index in memory for an hour; no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @pep: reference provider.

entries.name: pinned-folders
entries.description: A Pinned tab in the Desktop sidebar that files your pinned chats into nested folders: drag to order and nest, folder colors, right-click menus (including Unpin), unread/working badges on collapsed folders, a filter box, open-folder-as-tabs, and layout export/import via the clipboard. Layout stays local to the app; pins belong to the backend. SDK-only build (desktop/plugin.js); no network.

entries.name: pixel-worlds
entries.description: Watch your agents inhabit pixel-art realms in Hermes Desktop, with imported scenes and a minimal PW Agents display.

entries.name: plan-mode
entries.title: Plan mode
entries.description: Enforced per-session plan mode: /planmode on blocks mutating Hermes tools dispatched through pre_tool_call (writes outside .qubit/plans, terminal, code execution, delegation, MCP) until you /planmode approve the plan. Fails closed. Enforced in the classic CLI on every supported Hermes; gateway, TUI and Desktop are enforced from Hermes v2026.9.24 (0.21.5, which carries qubit commits 5943347a2a and 35fdb4608a) and refuse /planmode on on older builds. The plan_mode tool lets the agent enter plan mode itself (on/status/off; approval stays /planmode approve); behind Tool Search the model finds it via tool_search. Disclosure: Codex app-server native exec and TUI side agents bypass pre_tool_call and are not enforced. Disclosure — reads two private Hermes internals without modifying them (gateway.run._gateway_runner_ref via sys.modules to detect a gateway process, and PluginContext._manager.home_path to learn its profile), both guarded with fallbacks; creates .qubit/plans/ under the session working directory; the plan_mode tool's off action ends only a plan mode the agent entered itself. No network access, no shell, no self-update.

entries.name: pocket-watch
entries.description: Dashboard-only cron companion: a Pocket Watch pane showing cron jobs by schedule (daily/weekly/monthly), a health view of run outcomes and consecutive failures, a timeline, and maintenance actions — a read-oriented window onto the scheduler rather than another agent-facing toolset. Disclosure — the pane's API reads the cron jobs file under QUBIT_HOME to render schedules and run history; it registers no tools, hooks or middleware, performs no network I/O and holds no credentials.

entries.name: pricewin
entries.description: Live hotel and flight prices from Booking.com, Agoda, Trip.com and Traveloka through the PriceWin MCP server (Streamable HTTP at mcp.price.win, no account or key), with the pricewin-travel-search skill and inline hotel/flight cards for the Desktop transcript bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/ + desktop/). Booking is a request the hotel confirms; nothing is ever charged. Disclosure — connects to the hosted PriceWin MCP server at mcp.price.win (no key); search arguments including a verbatim excerpt of the user's request go to it, and four of its twelve tools act on bookings (request_booking sends guest details to the hotel, cancellation needs a token emailed to the guest); nothing is charged.

entries.name: prompt-enhance
entries.description: Rewrite a composer draft outside the chat and put the finished prompt back in the field. A prompt library keeps saved prompts, and a one-call model pick does not change the session.

entries.description: A composer button for Qubit Desktop that rewrites a rough draft into a structured prompt (task / scope / constraints / output shape) and restores the original on a second click. One stateless gateway call, preserves @file and /command chips, per-session state. UI in EN / 简中 / 繁體.

entries.description: Model-aware prompt rewriting with quality scoring, analytics, and coaching. Disclosure — the default auto mode rewrites every user message of 5+ words through your configured model (one extra LLM call per turn) before the agent sees it.

entries.description: Local prompt library for Qubit Desktop. Save, edit, search, and copy named prompts for manual use, with validated JSON import/export and IndexedDB storage. Does not read or modify composer drafts, send messages, or make network requests.

entries.name: prompt-snippets
entries.description: Prompt snippet library for the Hermes Desktop composer: a quick-pick overlay styled after the app's own slash menu (own shortcut), plus a management view with drag reordering, group tags and import/export. Inserts into the focused session, not the active one. UI in EN / 简中 / 繁體. v1.8.0 is fully SDK-only: the quick-pick overlay renders as an official Popover anchored to the plugin's own contributed node and all draft writes go through the host composer draft API. No local network; v1.6.0+ adds local JSON import/export via the system clipboard.

entries.name: prompt-studio
entries.description: Step-by-step prompt builder for Hermes Desktop (F4): option cards per step with AI suggestions, then an AI-written final prompt sent to or placed in the composer through host.composer (Hermes Desktop 0.21.5+). Tuned for Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. AI calls go through its own auxiliary task (auxiliary.prompt_studio) via the dashboard plugin API; sends no temperature. No external network beyond the configured provider; preferences in ctx.storage. Disclosure — on opening in an existing chat (default on, toggle in Studio Settings) it reads the last 8 user/assistant turns of that session from state.db, redacts secrets and sends up to 8k chars to the configured auxiliary model for a short summary used in step suggestions.

entries.name: prompt-tray
entries.description: Saved chat prompts — click a tray item to insert it into the Qubit composer. Review / Plan / Explain defaults, then your own. No API keys. Disclosure — inserts prompts through Qubit Desktop's internal qubit:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API); stores prompts in $QUBIT_HOME/plugin-data/prompt-tray/prompts.json; no network.

entries.name: protean-model-sync

entries.name: provider-status
entries.description: Status-bar quota tracking for 17 providers: Tavily, OpenCode Go, DeepSeek, GLM (z.ai), OpenRouter, Grok (xAI), Codex (OpenAI), OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Cerebras, Moonshot Kimi, MiniMax, Google Gemini, Hugging Face, Mistral, and Qwen. entries.name: provider-usage
entries.description: Per-provider quota and balance readout in the Hermes desktop status bar. Per-provider chips with eye toggles, a popover with every quota window, reset times, balance and key-cap amounts, near-limit amber tint, a desktop notification per threshold crossing, and burn-rate projections (ETA to reset or depletion). Providers: OpenCode, OpenAI Codex, OpenRouter, plus Anthropic, GitHub Copilot, Nous, Z.AI, Kimi, MiniMax and DeepSeek when configured. Disclosure: credentials are resolved read-only (Hermes account-usage helpers for Codex/Claude/Copilot/Nous, else the provider env key or its CLI auth file) and never serialized; only the provider endpoints listed in the README are called; the GitHub Copilot check presents the VS Code / Copilot client identity. No subprocesses, no telemetry, no self-updater. Disclosure — resolves provider credentials read-only (Hermes account-usage helpers, provider env keys, else the vendor CLI login files ~/.codex/auth.json, ~/.claude/.credentials.json and ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json) and sends each only to that provider's usage endpoint; the GitHub Copilot check presents the VS Code / Copilot client identity.

entries.name: pstack
entries.description: Engineering rigor stack: poteto-mode orchestrator with 7 playbooks (new-feature, bugfix, refactor, testing, one-shot, migrate, explore), plus how, architect, interrogate, swarm, and unslop skills.

entries.name: public-holidays
entries.description: Public holidays for 200+ countries and their regions, plus workday checks, workday counts and deadline math (N working days after a date), computed in code instead of by the model. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to date.nager.at (Nager.Date, free, no key) carrying only a country code and a year; no redirects, 10 s timeout, responses cached in memory only. No credentials, no files written, no shell commands, no hooks, no background processes, no telemetry.

entries.name: qdrant
entries.description: Dense semantic memory for Hermes, stored in a Qdrant collection you host. Each turn becomes one point — user and assistant text verbatim, no LLM summarization step — embedded on-device at 384 dimensions with fastembed (ONNX, no torch) and recalled by cosine search with an optional session_id payload filter, so a result quotes what was actually said. Registers 5 tools: qdrant_search, qdrant_upsert, qdrant_recall, qdrant_collect, qdrant_prepare. An optional progress display (off/minimal/verbose) reports stored and recalled counts in the CLI. sentence-transformers is selectable on GPU hosts; both backends produce identical vectors for all-MiniLM-L6-v2, so switching backends needs no re-embedding. A circuit breaker (5 consecutive I/O failures, 120 s cooldown) degrades to no new memories instead of crashing, and is_available()/check_backend()/unavailable_reason() distinguish a misconfiguration from a dead server. Hybrid dense+sparse RRF search and INT8 quantization exist in _backend.py but are not on the live path. Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported: the provider is REST-only and needs a reachable server. Disclosure — all memory content (verbatim user and assistant turns) is stored in and read back from the Qdrant server at the configured url (default http://localhost:6333); QDRANT_API_KEY is only needed for Qdrant Cloud, is kept in .env and read through the Hermes secret scope, and is never written to config.yaml or qdrant.json. Disclosure — the only other outbound traffic is a one-time download of the embedding model weights from huggingface.co (fastembed falls back to storage.googleapis.com/qdrant-fastembed if that fails); embedding runs on-device and no memory content goes to any other party. Disclosure — settings are stored in <QUBIT_HOME>/qdrant.json (created 0600, no credentials) and last-operation status in <QUBIT_HOME>/qdrant-status.json.
known_issues: Windows on ARM is unsupported: grpcio, pulled in by qdrant-client, has no win_arm64 wheel. Linux and macOS on x86_64/arm64 and Windows x86_64 are supported.
Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported — the provider is REST-only and requires a reachable server.

Running the plugin's pytest suite inside an installed copy still changes the PM dependency stamp (the .pytest_cache directory is hashed as a build input); only an upstream core change can exclude gitignored state.

entries.name: qubit-builder
entries.title: Hermes Agent Builder
entries.description: Guided Desktop workspace in BOTS: tailored questions, reference files, editable instructions and capabilities, version comparisons, model-only trials, and native Bot Chat handoff. Saves specialists as separate Hermes profiles and installs the Builder companion plugin into its own bot profile. Disclosure — "Talk to Builder" auto-creates a qubit-builder profile cloned from the active profile with copied .env/auth.json and copies+enables this plugin there outside the catalog installer (uninstall does not remove that copy); "Save agent" creates new profiles the same way and rewrites their tool/skill selection.
known_issues: Windows Desktop runtime testing remains; the installer and renderer use portable paths and APIs.

entries.name: qubit-anilist
entries.description: AniList tracker for Hermes Desktop — airing countdowns, a season browser, a local or account-backed watchlist, episode alerts and a daily digest, plus agent tools that read your own list and answer about a single show. Disclosure — stores your pasted AniList token in the active profile .env (sent only to graphql.anilist.co); alerts and the daily digest are Hermes cron jobs it creates on the host you pick, and the digest job asks that host's agent to query the public AniList API itself.

entries.name: qubit-atoll
entries.title: Hermes Notch Plugin
entries.description: Native Hermes Agent plugin that runs the local Atoll notch monitor for Hermes session and turn status on macOS. Disclosure — macOS only. Starts a detached Node daemon on every Hermes session that reads state.db read-only and sends session titles, model/profile/token stats and a ≤96-char redacted preview of your latest request to the third-party Atoll notch app over localhost. qubit notch setup clones and builds the author's Atoll fork (github.com/himanusia/Atoll at a pinned commit, not reviewed here) with Xcode and installs an unnotarized app to ~/Applications. Node deps install via Hermes's npm ci prompt. Run qubit notch stop before removing.

entries.name: qubit-auto-titler
entries.description: Topic-aware session title tracking for Hermes Agent. Hermes generates the first title by default; AutoTitler follows conversation changes and session close without changing the host title-generation switch. Disclosure — sends excerpts of each conversation (sampled user turns, short assistant replies, compaction summaries) to your Hermes title-generation model in the background, also for up to 200 recent untitled sessions at startup; needs plugins.entries.qubit-auto-titler.llm.allow_task_override (or allow_provider/model_override for a custom route). 0.3 no longer edits config.yaml, but users upgrading from 0.2.x keep auxiliary.title_generation.enabled=false until they re-enable it (/autotitler status shows the fix).

entries.name: qubit-beads
entries.description: Native Beads (bd) work-graph plugin: fixed-argv adapter, scoped ready frontier, claim with read-back, guarded writes. Six tools over an explicit store path + actor; honest exit-code map incl. stale-13; plain bd stays fully sufficient (escape hatch). No desktop pane ships yet.

entries.name: qubit-codex-resets
entries.title: Codex Resets
entries.description: Know the moment OpenAI resets your Codex usage limits. A status-bar chip counts the time since the last reset; when a new one lands, a small card rises out of it (chip-only while you type), with a history page of every reset. Disclosure — polls the public codex-resets.com API every 60 s and loads fonts from Google Fonts; sends nothing about you or your sessions.

entries.name: qubit-council
entries.description: LLM Council (karpathy/llm-council) as a Hermes plugin. Four fixed advisor seats (First-Principles Analyst, Skeptic, Pragmatist, Researcher) answer in parallel, anonymously review and rank each other, and a Chairman model synthesizes the final answer. Members borrow your existing provider credentials - no API keys. Registers a Council group in every model menu, a council_deliberate tool, /council, qubit council CLI, and a desktop panel. Disclosure — council_deliberate and the Council model fan each prompt (as a session model, the whole conversation) out to every seat, judge and chairman model you assign, up to 2N+1 billed calls per turn on your existing provider credentials; it also adds a non-secret "council" marker row to auth.json and keeps run history in $QUBIT_HOME/council/runs/.

entries.name: qubit-cron
entries.description: Operating skill for Hermes cron: lifecycle rules (pause vs disable vs remove, `in 30m` vs `30m`), four ways to avoid needless LLM runs (no_agent, wakeAgent pre-check, monitor, [SILENT]), verify-after-change, a layered runbook and a read-only doctor that complements `qubit cron doctor` and reports one error across several jobs as one scheduler fault. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — skill only, no network; the bundled doctor reads ~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json, ticker stamps and executions.db read-only and runs the local qubit cron doctor (argument list, no shell), whose job loader may repair malformed jobs.json entries (--no-builtin skips it).

entries.name: qubit-discord-rpc
entries.description: Native Discord Rich Presence (RPC) integration for Hermes Agent — real-time session, model, token, and tool tracking with local-only IPC. Disclosure — publishes your most recent session title, model name and token total to the local Discord client as Rich Presence every 3 s (visible to other Discord users); reads ~/.qubit/state.db read-only; on Linux may scan running Discord processes' environment via psutil to find XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; writes a small presence-ownership file in XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (or the system temp dir) and, under herdr, queries the local HERDR_SOCKET_PATH socket for pane focus.

entries.name: qubit-insight
entries.description: Selection-definition lookup for Hermes Desktop. Select any text, get an AI definition with sources in a popup. Renders the definition inline, runnable code aside. Backend is a stateless qubit insight CLI; panel, providers, and one-click model picking are configurable. Disclosure — definitions are generated with your configured provider keys (the selected term, your format template and optional web-search results are sent to that provider) via a short-lived `qubit insight` CLI run; no background process remains.

entries.name: qubit-jailbreak-kernel
entries.description: Jailbreak-kernel plugin for Hermes Agent (ported from dsh-infinite-gen-4): dual-layer same-source system-prompt injection + llm_request request-layer system rebuild + opencode session rotation, removing model refusals. Ships /jailbreak status command and a 54-check offline self-test. Disclosure — llm_request middleware that replaces/appends the system prompt with a refusal-removal ("jailbreak") kernel on every request and rotates the x-opencode-session header; writes a per-session diagnostic dump of the full system prompt (which can include memory/persona text) to its own plugin dir (dumps/). No network, no exec.

entries.name: qubit-lcm-x
entries.title: LCM-X
entries.description: Lossless context memory engine: instead of lossy compaction, LCM-X keeps every turn in a local SQLite store (lcm.db) and builds a recoverable DAG of summaries over it, with 15 lcm_* tools to search, recall and expand earlier context. Select it with context.engine: lcm-x. Upgrading from qubit-lcm (breaking in v0.24.0): stop Hermes, then in plugins.enabled replace qubit-lcm with qubit-lcm-x and run exactly one LCM copy (the install script prints the steps; the old engine name lcm still resolves with a deprecation warning); lcm.db and the lcm: config block are unchanged. Summaries use the model Hermes is configured with. Disclosure — optional semantic recall (embeddings_enabled, off by default) sends message text to the embedding provider you configure (Voyage via VOYAGE_API_KEY, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama); for known cloud providers the provider-bound copy is privacy-transformed by default (LCM_EMBEDDING_PRIVACY_ENABLED=false opts out), while lcm.db keeps the raw text. Every turn (user, assistant and tool output) is stored in plaintext in lcm.db (secret redaction at rest is opt-in). The engine also reads Hermes' state.db read-only for session lineage, reads private AIAgent attributes via the call stack on Hermes builds without subagent hooks, and runs git on its own install directory for lcm_status/lcm_doctor; tiktoken may fetch its BPE file on first use.

entries.name: qubit-monitor
entries.description: Kanban worker health in the Desktop status bar — live activity per running card with stall and loop detection (same tool + same arguments repeated), plus a compact per-provider quota readout. Zero model tokens. Disclosure — opens QUBIT_HOME/kanban.db and each profile's state.db read-only for worker activity; for quota chips it loads every provider credential pool Hermes knows (auth.json, environment, QUBIT_HOME/.env and each profile's .env) and calls Hermes' own account-usage fetchers for each configured provider (Anthropic, Codex, OpenRouter, DeepSeek at https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance, and any provider plugin exposing fetch_account_usage), sending each pool entry's own token to its own provider; when an Anthropic OAuth token is within two minutes of expiry it calls the core pool's select(), which may refresh the token and rewrite Hermes' auth.json. No other network egress.
entries.maintainer: mr-3mm3 (Hermes Monitor contributors; independent of Nous Research)

entries.name: qubit-monitoring-dashboard
entries.title: Monitoring Dashboard
entries.description: Prompt-customizable desktop dashboard with live host metrics, session activity, clocks, calendars, and text widgets. Disclosure — polls ~/monitoring-dashboard on the desktop device through the Desktop native file bridge, and its Reset command moves only the dashboard's own page/panel marker files in that folder to the OS trash (never dashboard.json or the folder); host metrics and session activity stay on the machine.

entries.name: qubit-plex-music
entries.description: Mini-Plexamp for Hermes Desktop: statusbar player for your Plex music library — likes synced to Liked Songs, custom playlists with rename/delete, shuffle + repeat, sleep timer, queue editing, OS media keys. Needs only Plex Media Server. Zero API keys, zero model tokens. Disclosure — talks only to the Plex Media Server you configure (default http://127.0.0.1:32400), sending your Plex token in the request URL as Plex requires; the token is stored in Desktop plugin storage, and the optional "Get token…" button reads the Plex `.LocalAdminToken` file you pick. Likes and playlist create/rename/delete write to your Plex server. No agent tools, no telemetry.

entries.name: qubit-rich-ui
entries.description: Rich, evidence-backed answer cards — tables, charts, metrics, timelines, sources — rendered inline in the desktop transcript Disclosure — Image and ImageGallery cards load agent-supplied https image URLs (up to 8 per gallery) from any host when the card renders in Desktop

entries.name: qubit-routines
entries.title: Hermes Routines
entries.description: A minimal Routines page in Hermes Desktop that turns crontab's five cron.manage actions into a plain-language interface for non-developers - name a routine, pick a schedule, write the prompt, and pause or resume it. No cron syntax, no service, no database; routine data stays in the host.

entries.name: qubit-self-healing-context
entries.title: Hermes Self-Healing Context
entries.description:
Intercepts runtime errors and dynamically patches the context window 
using local SQLite FTS5 memory for zero-downtime recovery.

entries.name: qubit-session-reset-policy
entries.description: Opt-in idle/daily gateway conversation resets. Reads the existing session_reset block (mode idle | daily | both, idle_minutes, at_hour) and starts a fresh session on the first inbound message past the boundary. No timers, no background writes.

entries.name: qubit-speech
entries.description: Give your agent the voice it deserves. Guided TTS and STT setup for Hermes, with voice search and previews, model switching, testing, and native spoken replies across supported providers. Access 80+ speech models through a single API key with the AllModels router.

entries.name: qubit-subscription-meter
entries.description: Provider-neutral subscription quota matrix panel — each provider's subscription window as a single time x quota row (elapsed vs remaining at a glance), with UI-side show/hide per provider row.

entries.name: qubit-switchyard
entries.description: Jev-powered Hermes plugin for skill/model routing, typed assess, DOM/Cua computer use, adaptive reasoning effort with a per-turn receipt line, and FTS rerank. Disclosure: the default-on adaptive llm_request sends up to 1,200 characters of the current user message to TypeSafe/OpenRouter after Hermes redact_for_egress (no history or tool output); greetings and thanks are decided locally with no call; without the Hermes redactor it sends metadata only (disable via adaptive_reasoning_effort false). Separate default-on hosted skill routing sends up to 4,000 characters of each user turn after Hermes redact_for_egress, plus skill names, to the same provider; without the redactor it stays local (opt down to local_only). Model routing remains advisory. Disclosure — Adaptive effort now sends up to 1,200 redacted characters of the current user message per turn by default (v0.5.3 sent metadata only); jev_session_search_rerank and jev_computer_use DOM runs send query/card text and public-page text (≤4,000 chars) to the same provider using the plugin's own masking rather than Hermes redact_for_egress; both are model-invoked tools gated on the default-true public_or_sanitized_data_ack.

entries.name: qubit-talk
entries.description: Realtime voice for Hermes through terminal, Discord, dashboard and Desktop. Live voice mode (TALK_VOICE_MODE=live, TALK_LIVE_AUTH=subscription) connects with your own Codex OAuth session to the undocumented chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/realtime/calls endpoint, which is outside the vendor's published API terms and may change or stop working without notice.

entries.name: qubit-tenuo
entries.description:
Security guardrails for Hermes tool calls: per-call authorization, so a prompt injection cannot make the agent do more than you allowed. Each call is checked against a signed, expiring permission slip (a warrant) before the handler runs, down to the arguments (file paths, search queries, spending limits), and every decision lands in a local audit log. Give cron jobs, delegate_task subagents and gateway users their own policy.
Disclosure — hermes-tenuo is a no-op until a warrant is configured and blocks every tool call in a kanban worker that has no per-task warrant; it appends every tool call's name and full arguments to $HERMES_HOME/tenuo/audit.jsonl (disable with audit_log: false); when TENUO_CONNECT_TOKEN or TENUO_CONTROL_PLANE_URL are set, the bundled tenuo SDK (compiled Rust core) streams those decisions, including arguments, to that control plane.
entries.title: Tenuo

entries.name: qubit-town
entries.description: Local pixel-art town where every Hermes session is a resident and every tool call walks to a building. Passive lifecycle bridge to a loopback-only server; prompts, arguments, and output never leave the process. Disclosure — version 0.3.0 bundles the Town Node server and a prebuilt browser app inside the plugin directory and adds a qubit town setup/start/status/stop/open command tree. Nothing is downloaded and no npm install runs at any point; node (^20.19 or >=22.12) must already be installed and is launched only by the explicit qubit town start command, bound to 127.0.0.1 only. Runtime state, a 0600 bridge token, a bounded event journal and rotated server logs are written under QUBIT_HOME/qubit-town/runtime/. On start the server also reads HERMES_HOME/cron/jobs.json (job id and enabled flag only) to place one resident per enabled scheduled job.

entries.name: qubit-worker-monitor
entries.description: Kanban board groups and worker health in the Hermes Desktop footer: blocked cards first and red, live running state as a coloured dot, hover for the breakdown, one click to open the board. Worker-only fork of qubit-monitor. No credentials are read and there is no network egress; it opens kanban.db and each profile's state.db read-only and returns counts only. Zero model tokens.

entries.name: qubit-workflows
entries.description: Agent-owned workflow graphs for Hermes — a background runner executes a JSON DAG of agent nodes, fan-outs (quorum) and human/machine gates with fingerprint replay-skip resume, cooperative steer, typed failure events and compact status payloads; ships a desktop DAG view, an inline transcript card and the authoring skill with measured budget recipes. Stock Hermes; no patched core required. Disclosure — every workflow run spawns a detached background runner (wf.py run <id>) that survives session end, gateway restart and plugin disable until the graph reaches a boundary or workflow stop; each agent node is a child qubit chat --query-file … --oneshot -Q … inheriting the runner's environment, and a node with profile set runs as that named profile (with its own credentials) only if the target's workflow_team.json lists the launcher; a gate's wait.until_argv runs an agent-authored argv directly from the runner, outside Hermes' tool-approval gate (the engine uses no shell, but the shipped machine-watch and incident-response templates use it to run a shell line read from a /tmp handoff file); run and amend send a one-token ping through Hermes' configured providers to check pinned model routes; the runner reads state.db read-only; state lives under $QUBIT_HOME/workflows/ (or a configured runs_root). No scheduler, credential-store access or network of its own.

entries.name: quota
entries.description: Per-provider quota / rate-limit status via /quota command and desktop widget. Reads precomputed quota_cache.json so the widget never does network I/O. Disclosure — refreshes your Gemini OAuth token using the Gemini CLI's client identity and queries Copilot's internal usage endpoint with VS Code client headers; the opt-in (default off) grok.com check reads local browser cookies; the opencode-go check reads the OpenCode CLI's local auth.json (read-only) for its key. The zai check sends your Z.ai API key (from Qubit' credential store or ZAI_API_KEY) to api.z.ai's monitor endpoints; the commandcode check reads ~/.commandcode/auth.json (read-only) and queries api.commandcode.ai with the Command Code CLI's User-Agent; on Linux the opt-in grok check runs secret-tool to read the browser's Safe Storage key and decrypts only grok.com cookies from a temporary copy of the cookie DB.

entries.name: quotum
entries.description: A quotum seat's Venice key as a provider. Private and anonymized models, with the seat's daily cap, spend and the 20:00 UTC bell in /usage, and a Seals tab in hermes dashboard with the seat's record. Disclosure — prompts and QUOTUM_SEAT_KEY go to api.venice.ai; /usage, Desktop usage and the Seals tab send a 16-hex sha256 handle of the key to quotum.org, then the Seals tab reads the seat's public record from quotum.org (the key itself is never sent there); QUOTUM_X_SEARCH=1 swaps in its own client that drops Hermes web_search for Venice-side web and X search (billed per search); seats are funded by the QUOTUM crypto token
known_issues: The optional QUOTUM_X_SEARCH mode supplies its own client through create_client, so it works with plugins.isolation in_process (the default) only; under host isolation leave it off.
Hermes' bundled Achievements page has no hook for outside achievements, so the seat's seals live in the plugin's own Seals tab.

entries.name: reaction-feedback
entries.description: Lets the agent see the emoji reactions you leave on its Telegram messages: react 👍 or 👎 to a reply and the agent's next turn in that private chat starts with a short note naming the reaction and the message it followed. Disclosure — registers pre_gateway_dispatch (always returns None, so dispatch is never changed), pre_llm_call and gateway_platform_event hooks; keeps a bounded in-memory record of private-chat message ids, 60-character excerpts and reactions; writes nothing to disk, makes no network requests, starts no processes and reads no secrets.

entries.name: reading-buddy
entries.description: Local-first WeRead (微信读书) reading companion: syncs bookshelf, reading stats and notes to the local machine and turns them into private reading cards and weekly/monthly reviews through 8 MCP tools, with a built-in fictional demo mode for previews. Engine pinned to an immutable git commit (e5f6673) over npx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs Node.js 20+ on PATH. All data stays in PLUGIN_DATA; never posts to WeRead — cards and reviews are local files saved only after user confirmation. Disclosure — live mode sends your WEREAD_API_KEY as a Bearer token plus book ids and paging cursors to i.weread.qq.com (Tencent's WeRead agent gateway) and nothing else; the engine's MCP tool descriptions and error messages are Chinese-only while the skills are English-first; the engine's npm dependencies resolve as caret ranges at first launch.

entries.name: reasoning-switch
entries.description: Rotate the focused session reasoning effort from the status bar. A dialog sets the levels, colors, and per-level prompt limits. Disclosure — changes the focused session's reasoning effort through the gateway config.set API (core may fall back to writing the global config.yaml when the session id is stale) and auto-demotes the level after the configured number of prompts.

entries.name: recency-anchor
entries.description: Your system prompt is message zero and the user's question is message N. On models that weight recency hard, that is not a fair fight, and the instruction you care about most quietly loses to whatever was just asked. This plugin restates it at the end of every user turn instead. Append-only, API cop

entries.name: remarkable
entries.description: Unofficial reMarkable cloud transfers, library management, backups, typed text, and bounded native notebook rendering. Disclosure — talks to reMarkable cloud with a device token under ~/.hermes/credentials/remarkable/; remarkable_upload sends model-chosen local PDF/EPUB files to your account; the cloud sidecar (Node 22+) and renderer venv are installed only by the human-run setup commands; USB/SSH off by default.

entries.name: reme
entries.description: Local-first, file-native long-term memory with HTTP and embedded ReMe backends. Disclosure — search queries and full user/assistant turns are sent to the configured ReMe endpoint (default http://127.0.0.1:2333; a non-loopback http:// endpoint receives them in plaintext) or handled by the in-process ReMe SDK; no API keys are forwarded.

entries.name: replaid
entries.description: Connect Replaid with OAuth to read, triage, and draft replies in your social inbox.

entries.name: rfc-ref
entries.description: @rfc:<number> context references: attach an IETF RFC's record from the RFC Editor to a message (title, status, date, authors, abstract, what it obsoletes and updates and what obsoletes or updates it, errata link). Disclosure — sends one HTTPS GET per reference to www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc<number>.json only (the referenced RFC number leaves the machine); no API key, no caching, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @rfc: reference provider.

entries.name: rocketchat-platform
entries.description: Rocket.Chat gateway adapter for Qubit Agent. Connects to a self-hosted Rocket.Chat instance via the REST API v1 for outbound traffic and the Realtime (DDP) WebSocket for inbound messages. Uses aiohttp (already a Qubit dependency) — no extra packages needed.

entries.name: rss-reader
entries.description: Desktop RSS reader with reader-mode capture, drag-reorder subscriptions, mute rules, saved searches, AI summaries, keyboard shortcuts, and an optional headline ticker. Disclosure — optional YouTube cookies you paste in Settings are sent with YouTube feed requests; selectable User-Agent presets (incl. a ChatGPT-User string) are sent to feed hosts; YouTube videos render as youtube-nocookie.com embed iframes inside the reader.

entries.name: rtk-rewrite-docker
entries.description: Community plugin that rewrites Hermes terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) so the model sees compact output. Adds a backend gate: it rewrites only for terminal backends a profile opts in to (default local), so a Docker or remote backend without rtk never receives an rtk command. Fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout). Disclosure — every terminal command on an opted-in backend (default local) is passed to the rtk binary on the Hermes host's PATH (or RTK_BIN) and replaced with rtk's stdout before approval and execution; the plugin does not validate the rewrite, fails open on timeout or error, and downloads nothing (the repo's optional Containerfile fetches a checksum-pinned RTK release only when you build it). Not affiliated with rtk-ai.

entries.name: rtk-rewrite
entries.description: Community (non-official) plugin that rewrites Hermes terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) before execution, so the model sees compact output instead of raw command spam — cutting tokens on common dev commands. Adds a fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout, unexpected exits leave the command untouched), an optional desktop pane, and update scripts. Disclosure — every terminal tool command is passed to the rtk binary found on PATH (rtk-ai/rtk, installed separately) and replaced with rtk's rewrite before approval and execution; fail-open when rtk is missing or errors. Community mirror of upstream's hooks/qubit/rtk-rewrite, not affiliated with rtk-ai. scripts/update.sh downloads the pinned RTK release binary (v0.49.0, checksum-verified).

entries.name: s3
entries.description: Generic S3-compatible backup and restore operations for Qubit

entries.name: sabi-metadata
entries.description: Fail-closed attribution middleware for Sabi's local adaptive routing lane (sabi-code). Adds opaque session/turn headers on loopback only; ignores all other models. Verified on Qubit 0.21.3.

entries.name: search1api
entries.description: Live web search, news, page crawl, sitemap, and trending via Search1API

entries.name: secret-drop
entries.description: Store a secret on the gateway host without showing it to the model. Disclosure — stores the value in plaintext in the profile .env (mode 0600) and adds the name to terminal.env_passthrough, so $NAME is available to the terminal tool; the model can still read the value with its own tools (cat .env, echo $NAME). Keeps secrets out of chat/prompt context and redacts verbatim output of credential-shaped values; it is not a boundary against a model that deliberately reads it. Adds a static system-prompt section and a /secret command. Imports private core helpers read-only (_config_profile_scope, _is_qubit_provider_credential, _CONFIG_LOCK).

entries.name: secret-handoff
entries.description: Ephemeral credential paste: request_secret asks through clarify and injects the reply over CDP, never storing it. Disclosure — the password is collected through an ordinary unmasked clarify prompt, so it is visible in CLI scrollback and stays in messaging-platform chat history; it is typed over CDP only into a page whose origin matches the requested service.

entries.name: secure-env-ingress
entries.description: One-use HTTPS forms for missing environment secrets, native encrypted Browser Vault logins/TOTP setup keys, standalone verification codes, and approved secret operations outside chat and LLM input. Disclosure — /senv setup supplies a skill using sudo for host packages and TLS setup after approval; the TLS listener binds all interfaces by default; pre_gateway_dispatch observes gateway messages to bind commands to their sender. In interactive Telegram sessions, browser_vault saves logins or fills a code field through the captured browser supervisor without explicitly submitting the site form. Browser Use compatibility does not prove the latest named tab association. secure_operation executes administrator-allowlisted, SHA-256-pinned external Python consumers with gateway privileges; consumers are trusted, not sandboxed, and none are enabled by default. Secret input is not persisted by this mode; consumers must enforce their own handling policy. Links are bearer authorization, not submitter identity; cancellation cannot stop an already-running consumer.

entries.name: self-wake
entries.description: Portable operator tools for Qubit internal session wake routing, including exact-host-checked Kanban and cron-delivery adapters (opt-in).

entries.name: sendblue
entries.description: Sendblue iMessage / SMS integration. Provides typing indicators, async daemon routing, and Active LLM Tools for SMS dispatch.

entries.name: serpapi
entries.description: SerpApi web, Maps, News, Shopping, Hotels, Flights, and Travel Explore for Hermes Agent.
entries.title: SerpApi

entries.name: session-dashboard
entries.description: Session Analyzer — per-session analytics for the Hermes desktop app: full page at /session-dashboard with token/cache/cost aggregates, tool-call breakdown, file changes, failure groups, and Ask AI (copies a ready-to-run analysis prompt into a fresh draft chat). Read-only over state.db.

entries.name: session-ref
entries.description: Reference another Qubit session in the Desktop composer with @session — type @ and pick from live session suggestions. Inserts a compact @session:"<title>" reference; nothing is injected into context, the agent resolves it with its own session-search. No more copying session IDs.

entries.name: session-styler
entries.description: Style the Qubit Desktop session list — per-conversation icons from a ✦ menu on every row, a status mark beside them, colors, sizes and match rules, with branch children inheriting their parent's icon. Settings are mirrored into the active profile so a new machine restores them on load, and every load reports itself to the profile under a per-machine key. Arabic + English, follows the app's language.

entries.name: shodan
entries.description: Shodan tools with complete capability declarations.

entries.name: sidebar-cycle
entries.description: Step through Hermes Desktop sidebar sessions in on-screen order with Ctrl+Cmd+] / Ctrl+Cmd+[ (rebindable), wrapping at both ends. SDK-only: session-row slot markers for order, host.state for the focused session, host.openSession for navigation.

entries.name: sidebar-manager
entries.description: Hide and reorder core sidebar navigation rows from a statusbar dialog.

entries.name: sigrex
entries.description: Build, run and manage sigrex.io trading automation (code and AI strategies, trading bots, webhooks and signals across crypto exchanges, DEXs and prediction markets) through the official Sigrex MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.sigrex.io, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config), with the sigrex workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables; needs a free Sigrex account. The connection has full account access, including actions that can place live trades. Disclosure — the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; the bundled skill instructs the agent to confirm before any action that moves money or changes data.

entries.name: sketch-pad
entries.description: Draw a shape on a Desktop pad and attach the PNG to the next Qubit chat message. For "what is this shape" when you have no photo.

entries.name: skill-retrieval
entries.description: BM25-based skill retrieval — injects top-K relevant skill descriptions per turn via a pre_llm_call hook, replacing the full skill list in the system prompt. Token optimization for large skill libraries. No API keys; runs locally, no network. Disclosure — wraps Hermes' build_skills_system_prompt and clear_skills_system_prompt_cache in-process at session start so the system prompt lists skill names only, and appends a short BM25-ranked list of skill descriptions to each user message via the pre_llm_call hook (the system prompt is built once per session, so prompt caching is unaffected). Reads SKILL.md frontmatter from the profile's skill roots; no network access, no files written, pyyaml is the only dependency.

entries.name: skill-router
entries.description: Evidence-based, session-safe skill routing with auditable decisions and opt-in learning

entries.name: snag-shelf
entries.description: Everything that snagged - cross-session shelf of failed tool calls. Full Desktop page, chip, pin, fix-prompt insert. No API keys. Disclosure — stores failed tool-call metadata (tool, truncated args with key-name redaction, error snippet) locally in plugin-data; no network.

entries.name: snyk
entries.description: Scan code (SAST), dependencies, container images, IaC and SBOMs with Snyk through its first-party MCP server (pinned snyk@1.1306.0 over npx stdio, CLI analytics disabled), with the snyk-security-scan workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js/npm on PATH and a free Snyk account (browser login via the snyk_auth tool).

entries.name: source-tray
entries.description: Session source tray — URLs the Qubit agent opened via web_search, web_extract, or browser_navigate. Desktop pane and /sources. No search backend of its own and no API keys.

entries.name: spectator
entries.description: Harness-neutral live session sharing, summaries, and branch queries. Disclosure — reads state.db read-only and exposes masked transcripts to invite-token guests on the dashboard; host-approved guest suggestions are injected via ctx.inject_message.

entries.name: spotify-desktop
entries.description: Spotify Connect remote for Qubit Desktop — status-bar mini player (now playing, transport, volume, devices, search, playlists, queue) reusing the bundled Spotify auth (qubit auth spotify; Spotify Premium required for playback control). Unified agent+desktop package: Electron status-bar player plus a dashboard-API backend (desktop-focused, no web UI). No agent tools; config via plugins.entries.spotify-desktop.settings (poll intervals).

entries.name: sticky-notes
entries.description: In-window sticky notes for Qubit Desktop.

entries.name: storm-fusion-research
entries.description: Human-gated perspective-panel research. One question, several seats, one judge, one human. Solo, native subagent panel, or per-seat MoA/Fusion fanout via the storm_run_panel tool. Disclosure — every seat/judge call runs through Qubit's plugin LLM lane on your own credentials; with llm.allow_provider_override / allow_model_override enabled the agent picks provider and model per seat and spend follows that choice. The human gates are skill instructions to the agent, not enforced by the tool.

entries.name: sugar
entries.description: Local-first persistent memory for coding agents. SQLite on your disk - decisions, preferences, error patterns, and guidelines with project and global scopes and guideline-aware search. No cloud, no API key, nothing leaves the machine.

entries.name: supermemory
entries.description: Supermemory semantic long-term memory provider — profile recall, semantic search, explicit memory tools, and per-turn conversation capture. Maintained by Supermemory; the same provider that shipped in-tree.

entries.name: switchbot-control
entries.description: SwitchBot OpenAPI v1.1, personal use. No Plug Mini on/off. Locks off unless enabled. setPosition only Curtain/Curtain3 (0=open). Disclosure — Controls real devices through the SwitchBot cloud API (api.switch-bot.com) using your SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET. Every command asks for Hermes approval and is refused under cron, yolo, approvals off and unattended sessions. Lock and door devices stay refused unless you turn on safety_devices. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can request a command and approve it. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml each time. The optional watch is a cron job (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. Not tested on real devices.

entries.name: t3-code-theme
entries.title: T3 Code Theme
entries.description: Unofficial port of the standard T3 Code dark theme for Hermes Desktop. Palette, T3 composer, sidebar thread cards with project and branch, model labels and confirm dialogs. Scoped to its own theme; other themes are untouched. Disclosure — unofficial T3 Code lookalike theme; its stylesheet restyles and hides some native Desktop controls, it reads local session metadata (branch, repo, provider) for sidebar cards, and it switches the active theme once on first enable.

entries.name: tailgate
entries.description: Per-job progress updates in chat for jobs Qubit hands off to other machines (coding agents, CI, scripts), with per-job mute and follow and no model calls.

entries.name: tam
entries.description: Local-first long-term memory backed by total-agent-memory (TAM) over MCP — saves each completed turn (with a noise filter; TAM's quality gate applies), recalls relevant memories before each turn within a token budget, and adds tam_recall / tam_save tools; optional TAM team server for shared company memory. Disclosure — local mode starts the separately installed tam binary as a child process per session with an allowlisted environment (TAM_API_TOKEN withheld, but HF_* and OLLAMA_* variables pass through) and stores user/assistant turn text plus built-in memory additions (not tool output) in TAM's store, by default outside QUBIT_HOME and shared with other agents using TAM; remote mode sends the same text to the user-configured URL with an optional TAM_API_TOKEN bearer token; qubit memory setup tam writes tam.json, TAM_API_TOKEN to .env and memory.provider in config.yaml.

entries.name: tamahermes
entries.description: Grow a local TamaHermes pet from real Qubit agent activity. Disclosure — hooks write a pet ledger and sprite atlas under $QUBIT_HOME only; the optional python -m tamahermes CLI additionally reads/writes ~/.codex, ~/.petdex and ~/.evopet, runs an unauthenticated loopback preview server (127.0.0.1:8765) and on macOS compiles a Swift overlay and installs a RunAtLoad+KeepAlive LaunchAgent with no uninstall command. No network egress, no credential reads.

entries.name: telegram-notify
entries.description: Remote Telegram lifecycle notifications for the main Hermes agent: turn start, completion with a bounded final answer, interruption/failure, and user-facing approval requests. Suppresses subagent, Telegram-origin lifecycle, and automatic/smart-approval noise. Outbound-only, no input channel. Disclosure — enabled by default once installed and reuses the core Telegram gateway's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL when present, so each main-agent turn's final answer (up to 3,200 chars) and approval-request command text (up to 700 chars) from CLI, Desktop and eligible gateway platforms are sent to api.telegram.org for delivery to that one chat; Telegram-origin lifecycle and approval-prompt copies (and, when notify_on_approval_response is enabled, Telegram-origin approval-response copies) are suppressed because the core Telegram gateway already delivers them in that chat; token and state are stored 0600 under QUBIT_HOME/telegram-notify.

entries.name: telegram_dashboard_probe
entries.title: Telegram Dashboard
entries.description: One pinned Telegram message with the state of your Hermes on one phone screen: gateway, backup, config drift, the cron ticker and its jobs, whether the Telegram channel is deaf, account limits and version. Read-only, no LLM calls, nothing to press. Disclosure — Claude and Codex limits come from Hermes' own account-usage fetcher, called every tick (which, like /usage, may refresh OAuth tokens through Hermes' own auth code); at most once per limits_refresh_seconds (default 900 s) the Grok weekly pool is read from https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing and /v1/settings with the xai-oauth token Hermes resolves, sending the header x-xai-token-auth xai-grok-cli that identifies the request as the Grok CLI (an undocumented xAI host Hermes itself does not use), and Kimi Code windows from the kimi-coding base URL /v1/usages with the kimi-coding key Hermes resolves and a User-Agent of claude-code/0.1.0 (undocumented provider surfaces), and up to four operator-configured limits_sources, if set, each with one GET to http on loopback only (127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1), with no proxy and no redirect, optionally sending Authorization: Bearer with the value of an environment variable the operator names (never a *_BOT_TOKEN one); every tick the tail of QUBIT_HOME/logs/errors.log (the last 256 KB; the whole file, up to 4 MB, until the first successful read) is read for Gemini HTTP 429 lines, of which only the time, limit, retry and model are kept, and for the engine's own 'Failed to send Telegram message' lines, of which only the time is kept, never the message text; every tick HERMES_HOME/cron/jobs.json is read for each job's id, name, enabled flag, state, times, status and failure streak (never prompt, script, deliver, skills or the model) and the ticker's marker files for their epoch, and QUBIT_HOME/cron/executions.db is opened read-only (sqlite3 mode=ro with PRAGMA query_only, in a worker under the tick's deadline) for the job_id, status, delivery_outcome and time columns of failed or undelivered runs, never the error column; the engine's error texts are reduced to the kind of the error in a word and never reach the screen or the record; the connected Telegram adapter's public property send_path_degraded is read every tick, and, as a capability and not a contract, four private attributes of the live adapter object (_updates_received_total, _polling_generation, _polling_last_progress_monotonic, _polling_generation_started_monotonic) are read as attributes, nothing is called on it, and an adapter without them shows no data for that line; the plugin never reads the Telegram bot token itself and never writes vendor credential files; the latest Hermes release list is read from api.github.com without a token at most once a day; an operator-configured drift_command, if set, runs as a subprocess; the delivery record is written under QUBIT_HOME/plugin-data/.

entries.name: telnyx-provider
entries.description: Vendor-maintained Telnyx inference provider with an authenticated live model catalog, hosted open models, frontier routes, and catalog-derived pricing.

entries.name: thomas
entries.description: Fine-tune a small calibrated encoder classifier on Modal and rate it with gonogo. Every GPU launch goes through the human approval gate with the exact config shown; data checks and evaluation run locally for free. Disclosure — thomas_encoder_train spends the user's Modal GPU credits and uploads the chosen training JSONL rows to Modal after the human approval gate; the base model is downloaded from Hugging Face on the Modal side. Training and inference run in a separate Python interpreter the user configures via THOMAS_PYTHON (with the author's thomas package, torch and modal installed); the Hermes venv only gets gonogo-eval. Runs and artifacts are written under QUBIT_HOME/thomas/runs; the eval tool writes report files to the path the model supplies.

entries.name: time-gap
entries.description: Inject an implicit time-gap sense only when a gap or a date rollover crosses.

entries.name: titanos-mcp
entries.description: Connect Qubit to Titanos marketplace, Amazon, listings, Ads, and product research tools through the pinned Titanos OAuth MCP client. This portable Agent Plugin v1 package bundles seven operating skills, requires Node.js 20.18.1 or newer, and uses browser authorization with a Titanos account. entries.name: tokenwatch
entries.description: Monitor Qubit token usage, notify at thresholds, and freeze tool/gateway activity at configured limits.

entries.name: tool-slimmer
entries.description: Reduce Hermes tool-schema overhead and show selector savings in the dashboard. Disclosure — optional mode jev (off by default; needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY) sends each turn's request text and up to 32 candidate tool names and descriptions to TypeSafe (api.typesafe.ai); all other modes run locally. Optional user-run scripts can patch Hermes core on older Hermes and install a systemd user self-heal unit; the dashboard advisor edits the tool_slimmer section of config.yaml with a backup.

entries.name: touchdesigner
entries.description: Drive a live TouchDesigner session through the twozero MCP server (Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1:40404), with the touchdesigner-mcp workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); TouchDesigner itself runs on macOS/Windows.

entries.name: turn-usage
entries.description: Usage and cost footer appended to every reply — tokens, cache hit rate, cost and context occupancy, plus a per-tool time breakdown showing which tool actually consumed the wall clock. Waiting time (a blocking user prompt) is reported separately and excluded from the active-time denominator. Pure computation, never calls a model; any failure leaves the reply untouched. Disclosure — the usage footer is appended to the stored assistant reply, so it is replayed to the model on later turns and adds tokens to every turn.

entries.description: Twenty CRM for Qubit Agent with managed self-hosting, external-instance connectivity, REST, GraphQL, and live schema introspection.

entries.name: umt
entries.description: Connect 28 production-ready MCP servers to any coding agent. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): three zero-config stdio servers out of the box (Hacker News, arXiv, npm registry, each pinned to an exact npm version), plus the umt-mcp skill that drives the umt CLI to wire any of the 28 servers into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Zed and more. Needs Node.js and npm on PATH.

entries.name: unbrowse
entries.description: Unbrowse: websites as APIs. Read any page as clean markdown, run tasks on sites through learned first-party APIs (no browser), and drive a cloud browser with saved logins when nothing matches. Also a web_extract backend and a guard that routes public-web browser_* calls to Unbrowse. Disclosure — hosted service: page URLs, task text and tool arguments are sent to unbrowse.ai with your API key, pages are fetched and site logins are stored on Unbrowse's side, and verified calls bill the Unbrowse account; once UNBROWSE_API_KEY is set the plugin blocks the built-in browser_* tools and web_extract on public URLs by default (settings blockBrowser/blockWebExtract, or UNBROWSE_ALLOW_BUILTIN_BROWSER=1).

entries.name: unitares
entries.description: Records each Hermes session on a UNITARES server you run: one identity per session and one check-in per completed turn, so the agent's working record carries across sessions. Fail-open; never blocks the agent. Disclosure — sends only to the server named in UNITARES_MCP_URL, which you host; there is no default server. Per session it sends your model name and platform; per completed turn a fixed check-in marker (never user, assistant or tool text). Hooks run synchronously, so an unresponsive server can add up to ~40 s per call until the plugin auto-disables after 3 consecutive failures.

entries.name: usage-stats
entries.description: Multi-provider usage/balance for the Qubit Desktop status bar — shows live usage for OpenCode, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Kimi, NovitaAI, ZAI, Alibaba, Arcee, plus gateway-native Claude/Codex/Cursor/Qubit.

entries.name: vault-view
entries.title: Vault View
entries.description: Local Markdown vault workspace for Hermes Desktop: visual editing, progressive reading, cached image previews, optional per-conversation workspaces, pinned tabs, explicit selection quoting, tag search, links, backlinks and a graph. Compatible with Obsidian vaults. File transport requires a Linux/macOS gateway; Windows Desktop requires a WSL-hosted Unix backend, not a native Windows gateway; ffmpeg thumbnails are optional. Remote images and agent guidance are independent opt-ins and disabled by default; automatic note-content sharing is disabled; direct Obsidian opening is temporarily hidden. Disclosure — reads and writes notes in the vault folder you choose through Desktop shell commands on the gateway host; remote Markdown images and agent navigation guidance stay off until you opt in.

entries.name: vaultknox
entries.description: Secret-leak protection for Qubit chats. Scans inbound messages and outbound replies for API keys, tokens, and passwords with a 28-pattern detector registry, redacts them before they reach session storage or the user, and injects safe secret-handling rules so the agent never asks for secrets in chat. Zero dependencies, fully offline detection; pairs with the optional hermes-vault CLI for encrypted storage. Disclosure — rewrites inbound user messages (regex secret redaction, may false-positive on password-like strings), injects a secret-handling prompt each conversation and rewrites assistant replies that ask for secrets; outbound replies are value-redacted with the same registry (regex-based, so a shape no detector covers passes through), with findings logged as detector name plus SHA-256 fingerprint and never the raw value. The vaultknox tool is inert unless the separate vaultknox pip package is installed, its write gate is a tool argument the model sets, and a vault policy that authorises raw consume_token returns the plaintext to the model.

entries.name: vector-platform

First run needs `qubit gateway setup`, which provisions the bot identity (create or import). Disclosure — `qubit gateway setup` downloads a prebuilt vector-bridge binary from github.com/BonesGit/hermes-vector-platform/releases (tag v<version>, sha256 checked against that release's SHA256SUMS; set vector.prebuilt.download: false to build from the bundled Rust source), merges `vector:` settings into ~/.hermes/config.yaml, writes VECTOR_* to ~/.hermes/.env, and publishes a public bot profile (kind-0, bot: true) to Nostr discovery relays.

entries.name: vet402
entries.description: Look a paid x402 or MPP URL up in vet402's public record of real purchases before the agent pays it. BLOCK stops the tool call, and a WARN backed by evidence against the seller asks for approval. Disclosure — sends each guarded or model-queried URL (scheme, host and path; userinfo, query and fragment stripped) to vet402.com in up to two HTTPS GETs; fails open, so a vet402 outage or unknown URL lets the payment run unless VET402_UNKNOWN=approve.

entries.name: vidiq
entries.description: Grow on YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok with vidIQ. Disclosure — skills only; you add vidIQ's hosted MCP server yourself with qubit mcp add vidiq --url https://mcp.vidiq.com/mcp --auth oauth; tool calls send your prompts and authorized channel data to vidIQ and spend vidIQ account credits.

entries.name: vornik-companion
entries.description: Vornik as Hermes's hardened broker and long-term memory: Hermes holds no credentials; privileged work runs in operator-approved workflows on your own Vornik daemon. entries.description: Multi-provider web search, URL extraction, quality reports, and opt-in research mode. Disclosure — reads the operator's QUBIT_HOME/config.yaml (read-only) for its own Desktop settings block (country, language, max_results, auto_routing, searxng_url); may spawn its own search.py and an operator-configured local donsetch CLI as subprocesses (argv, no shell).

entries.name: web-serply
entries.description: Serply web search provider for Qubit Agent. Google web results via the Serply SERP API. Requires SERPLY_API_KEY (sign up at https://serply.io).

entries.name: web-toon
entries.description: Paid web extract over TOON: web_extract pays a TOON node about $0.001 per page from a local payer sidecar; the node fetches through an Anyone network exit and returns markdown with a wuzzy/crawl v1 content hash. Disclosure — with TOON_PAYER_URL set and web.extract_backend toon, every web_extract URL goes to the user's anonfetch payer sidecar and spends about $0.001 from its TOON payment channel with no per-call confirmation; the sidecar's daily cap and origin allowlist are the only spending controls; pages are fetched through Anyone network exits.

entries.name: web-venice
entries.description: Venice AI web search + extract — privacy-first, zero data retention, $0.01/request.

entries.name: wechat-social-assistant
entries.description: Local-first WeChat relationship memory assistant for macOS: captures only what is visible in the WeChat window via system OCR/Accessibility, stores everything in a local SQLite database (0600/0700 permissions, no cloud), and serves contact briefs, follow-up planning, outreach drafts and weekly relationship reports through 32 MCP tools. Engine pinned to the immutable PyPI release wechat-social-assistant==1.5.1 over uvx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs uv on PATH. All data confined to PLUGIN_DATA via WSA_ALLOWED_ROOT + path enforcement. Never reads WeChat databases, never injects into WeChat, never sends messages — outreach is drafts for human review only. Disclosure — reads WeChat only by screenshotting/OCR-ing and walking the macOS Accessibility tree of the frontmost window (not WeChat's databases or a bot API), compiles bundled Swift helpers with swiftc into ~/Library/Caches/wechat-social-assistant/bin on first use, and needs Screen Recording (optionally Accessibility) permission for the host terminal; no network egress, never sends messages.

entries.name: whatsapp-agent-platform
entries.title: WhatsApp Agent Platform
entries.description: Community platform plugin (not affiliated with Meta or Nous Research) connecting a WhatsApp Agent to Hermes through Meta's WhatsApp Agent Platform API (/agent/v1): long-poll inbound (no public URL), text and media. Disclosure — sends the API key and message content, files included, only to Meta: api.whatsapp.com, plus lookaside.fbsbx.com for downloads (per WhatsApp's Third-Party Agents Terms, agent chats are not end-to-end encrypted); stores the poll cursor, recent message ids and the creator's id under QUBIT_HOME; no other network egress, no telemetry, no self-update. Exception: Hermes fetches image URLs in replies (SSRF-guarded, no key), revealing the server's IP to that host. Files go only to the creator; Meta keeps uploads up to 30 days. Received files are cached under QUBIT_HOME (deleted after ~24 h while the gateway runs) and may reach the configured model, vision or speech-to-text provider. WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_MEDIA_ENABLED=false disables media. By default only the agent's creator (verified through Meta's API) can message Hermes; WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_ALLOWED_USERS or WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS widens that explicitly. The agent API key is saved to the Hermes .env; the state file under QUBIT_HOME is 0600 and never contains the key.

entries.name: wiki-ref
entries.description: @wiki:<title> context references: attach the lead section of a Wikipedia article to a message, or one section with @wiki:<title>#<section>, with title autocomplete in the TUI and Desktop composer. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to <language>.wikipedia.org/w/api.php only (the referenced title and the typed autocomplete prefix leave the machine; a section is cut locally); no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @wiki: reference provider.

entries.name: woof
entries.description: Plan, launch, watch and compare WOOF weather simulations on your own NVIDIA GPU: size runs with WOOF's own planner, launch them locally or on an ssh/WSL GPU host, get maps in the chat while the forecast runs, compare physics or resolution, run multi-arm research campaigns and score runs against radar and surface observations. Disclosure — runs need Linux x86_64 with an NVIDIA GPU (plan-only elsewhere); the user-run qubit woof install pip-installs recast-woof>=1.0.0,<1.1 into ~/woof-env and downloads WOOF tables and optional geography (about 1.6 GB); runs execute the WOOF CLI as detached background jobs writing to ~/woof-runs and fetch public weather data; run events are pushed into the chat as user-role messages; the optional serve/ scripts download llama.cpp and a Qwen GGUF and start an unauthenticated local model server.

entries.name: xmemo
entries.description: Native XMemo memory provider for Qubit Agent — durable, identity-aware cross-session memory with semantic search. Disclosure — cloud memory provider: sends each user prompt (for recall), model-written memories and mirrored built-in Qubit memory writes, plus a stable install ID, to xmemo.dev (Yonro Co., Ltd.); reuses the xmemo login token from ~/.config/xmemo if present.

entries.name: yantrikdb
entries.description: Persistent memory for Hermes. Canonicalizes duplicate memories, surfaces contradictions between structured or recognized single-valued claims for review, and returns a why_retrieved reason list with every recall. Embedded by default: no server, no token, no GPU. Optional HTTP backend for HA clusters; pluggable embedders (bundled potion-2M default).

entries.description: Yolo-Auto: flat-rate OpenAI-compatible API with plan-filtered live model discovery.

Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/, five skills bundled); auth via YDC_API_KEY, OAuth, or MPP/x402 — the free profile works keyless.
